definition_zh: 悲伤；难过；令人悲伤的事
definition_en: the feeling of being sad; the quality of showing sorrow; a sad event or fact
core_image: 胸口发沉、眼泪将落未落的感觉
scene: 她眼中流露出深深的悲伤。 There was deep sadness in her eyes.
sceneCN: 这里 sadness 是「悲伤、难过」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她眼中流露出深深的悲伤。

derivatives.zh: 悲伤的；难过的
悲伤地；遗憾地
使悲伤；使难过

senses.title: The feeling of sorrow
senses.definition: the feeling of being unhappy and sorrowful
senses.definitionCN: 不快乐而又悲伤的感受
senses.example: A wave of sadness washed over him.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵悲伤涌上他的心头。
senses.why: The core sense is the inner state of sorrow.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是内心悲伤的状态。

senses.title: Outward sign of sorrow
senses.definition: the quality of looking or sounding sorrowful
senses.definitionCN: 神情或声音中流露出的悲伤
senses.example: There was sadness in her voice.
senses.exampleCN: 她的声音里带着悲伤。
senses.why: The inner state becomes visible to others.
senses.whyCN: 内心的状态变得让旁人看得见。

senses.title: A sad fact
senses.definition: something that makes people feel sorrow
senses.definitionCN: 使人感到悲伤的事情
senses.example: The sadness of the story stayed with me.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事的悲伤一直留在我心里。
senses.why: A state becomes a fact that can be named.
senses.whyCN: 状态变成可以被指称的事实。

intro.en: Sadness is sad plus the noun ending -ness, from Old English -nes.
intro.cn: sadness 由 sad 加名词词尾 -ness 构成，-ness 源自古英语 -nes。

items.en: The ending -nes forms nouns of state.
items.cn: 古英语词尾 -nes 构成表示状态的名词。

items.en: Sad still carries the sense of weary fullness.
items.cn: 当时的 sad 仍带有「饱足而倦」的含义。

items.en: Sadness names the state of being sorrowful.
items.cn: sadness 指悲伤的状态。

items.en: The word appears in poetry and letters.
items.cn: 这个词出现在诗歌与书信中。

items.en: Sadness covers feelings, signs, and sad facts.
items.cn: sadness 涵盖感受、表现与令人悲伤的事实。

note.en: Sadness is the state; sorrow is its deeper form.
note.cn: sadness 是悲伤的状态，sorrow 则是更深的悲痛。

entries.definition: the state of being mad
entries.definitionCN: 疯狂

entries.definition: the feeling of being glad
entries.definitionCN: 高兴

entries.definition: the quality of being bad
entries.definitionCN: 坏；恶劣

entries.definition: deep sadness
entries.definitionCN: 悲伤；悲痛

entries.definition: great sadness after a loss
entries.definitionCN: 失去亲人后的悲痛

entries.definition: the state of being unhappy
entries.definitionCN: 不快乐

normalIntro.en: Sadness names the feeling of sorrow and the signs it leaves.
normalIntro.cn: sadness 指悲伤的感受，也指它留下的种种表现。

normal.en: A deep sadness filled the empty house.
normal.cn: 深深的悲伤充满了空荡的房子。

normal.en: She could not hide her sadness.
normal.cn: 她无法掩饰自己的悲伤。

normal.en: There was sadness in his quiet voice.
normal.cn: 他平静的声音里带着悲伤。

normal.en: The sadness of the ending surprised us.
normal.cn: 结局的悲伤让我们感到意外。

normal.en: Music can express sadness without words.
normal.cn: 音乐可以不用语言表达悲伤。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy weight resting on the chest.
abstract.cn: 想象胸口压着一块沉重的石头。

abstract.en: Imagine tears that stop before they fall.
abstract.cn: 想象泪水将落未落。

abstract.en: Think of an empty room after a farewell.
abstract.cn: 想象告别之后空荡的房间。

examples.en: His sadness was clear to everyone.
examples.cn: 他的悲伤大家都看得出来。

examples.en: She wrote a poem about loss and sadness.
examples.cn: 她写了一首关于失去与悲伤的诗。

examples.en: The sadness of the news spread across the town.
examples.cn: 这个消息带来的悲伤传遍了小镇。

dict_mnemonic.text: sad 加名词后缀 -ness，表示「悲伤的状态」，就是 sadness。

root: 由形容词 sad 加名词词尾 -ness 构成，核心义「悲伤的状态及其表现」。

sensesIntro.en: Sadness means the feeling of sorrow, its outward signs, or a sad fact.
sensesIntro.cn: sadness 意为悲伤的感受、悲伤的表现，或令人悲伤的事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy feeling behind the eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：双眼里沉甸甸的感受。

branches.en: The base sense is the inner feeling.
branches.cn: 基础义是内心的感受。

branches.en: Feeling becomes visible in face and voice.
branches.cn: 感受在神情与声音中显现。

branches.en: Sorrow becomes a fact that can be named.
branches.cn: 悲伤变成可以被指称的事实。

branches.en: Inner sorrow and outward grief belong together.
branches.cn: 内心的悲伤与外在的哀伤相互关联。

branches.en: Visible grief and sad events often overlap.
branches.cn: 可见的哀伤与悲伤的事件常常重叠。

intro.en: Sadness is sad plus -ness, one of the most productive noun endings in English.
intro.cn: sadness 由 sad 加 -ness 构成，-ness 是英语中构词力很强的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Sadness has no Latin root; both sad and -ness are native English elements.
latinIntro.cn: sadness 没有拉丁词根；sad 与 -ness 都是英语本族成分。

items.exampleCN: 这个消息让全家很悲伤。

items.example: The room felt sadder at night.
It was the saddest day of the year.
items.exampleCN: 那是一年中最悲伤的一天。

items.example: A sad-eyed child stood at the door.
items.exampleCN: 一个眼神悲伤的孩子站在门口。
那位面带悲伤的女士向我们道谢。

definition_zh: 大量；许多；富足；足够地
definition_en: a large amount that is enough or more than enough, and informally an adverb meaning fully or very
core_image: 敞开的粮仓门，谷物堆成小山，多到不必去数
scene: 市集快散场时，果摊老板指着还剩大半的木箱，让你随便挑。 There is plenty of time, so nobody needs to hurry.
sceneCN: 这里是「大量、许多」的用法（第 1 个义项），出现在 plenty of 这一结构中；句意为时间很充裕，谁都不必赶。画面里有快收摊的果摊、半箱水果和不再着急的顾客。

derivatives.zh: 由 plenty 的词干加 -eous 构成，文学用语，义为「丰盛的；大量的」
借拉丁 plenitudo 而来，与 plenty 同源，义为「丰足；充满」

senses.title: A large amount
senses.definition: a quantity that is large and usually more than is needed, used with of before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 数量很大、通常超出所需的量，放在名词前时用 of 连接
senses.example: There is plenty of room for everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 地方很宽裕，谁都坐得下。
senses.why: The noun descends from a Latin word for fullness, so plenty names a container that is already full rather than a measured number.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词源自拉丁语中表示「满」的词，所以 plenty 说的是一个已经装满的容器，而不是量出来的数字。

senses.title: A condition of abundance
senses.definition: a state or period in which there is a lot of something, especially food or money
senses.definitionCN: 某样东西尤其是食物或钱财很多的状况或时期
senses.example: The old stories describe years of plenty followed by years of hunger.
senses.exampleCN: 古老的故事里，富足的年份之后接着是饥饿的年份。
senses.why: Once the noun names a full supply, it can also name the whole period that enjoys such a supply, which is how a time of plenty appears.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个名词能指「装得满满的供给」，也就能指享有这种供给的整段时期，于是有了「富足的岁月」这种说法。

senses.title: Enough, or very
senses.definition: used informally as an adverb to mean enough or very, as in plenty hot
senses.definitionCN: 非正式地用作副词，表示「足够」或「很」，如 plenty hot
senses.example: The soup is plenty hot for me.
senses.exampleCN: 这汤对我来说已经够烫了。
senses.why: Because plenty already means more than enough, the same form can modify an adjective and say that the degree is fully sufficient.
senses.whyCN: 既然 plenty 本身就表示「超出所需」，同一个形式就能去修饰形容词，说明程度已经完全够了。

intro.en: Plenty came into English through French from a Latin word for fullness, and it stayed a noun while its relative plentiful became the adjective.
intro.cn: plenty 经法语从表示「满」的拉丁词进入英语，一直保持名词身份，而它的同族词 plentiful 则成了形容词。

items.en: Plenus meant full, and it supplied the whole family of English words about abundance.
items.cn: plenus 意为「满的」，为英语里一整族表示「充足」的词提供了来源。

items.en: The noun plenitas meant fullness or completeness, the abstract state of being full.
items.cn: 名词 plenitas 意为「满、完备」，指装满这一抽象状态。

items.en: Old French plente kept the sense of abundance and was used of harvests, stores and wealth.
items.cn: 古法语 plente 保留了「充足」之义，用于收成、储备与财富。

items.en: Middle English borrowed plente as a noun and used it in phrases about food, money and time.
items.cn: 中古英语把 plente 借作名词，用于谈论食物、钱财与时间的词组。

items.en: Modern English fixed the spelling plenty and added the informal adverbial use, as in plenty hot.
items.cn: 现代英语把拼写固定为 plenty，并添上非正式的副词用法，如 plenty hot。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin full family around the noun; the near-meaning group gathers nouns for a large quantity.
note.cn: 形近组收围绕这个名词的拉丁语「满」词族；近义组收表示「大量」的名词。

entries.definition: The adjective formed from this noun with -ful.
entries.definitionCN: 由这个名词加 -ful 构成的形容词。

entries.definition: An older adjective meaning abundant.
entries.definitionCN: 较老的形容词，义为「丰盛的」。

entries.definition: A formal noun for fullness or completeness.
entries.definitionCN: 正式用语，指满盈、完备。

entries.definition: Full or complete, as of a session with everyone present.
entries.definitionCN: 完全的；全体出席的。

entries.definition: A very large quantity of something.
entries.definitionCN: 极大量的某物。

entries.definition: A large amount, as in a lot of time.
entries.definitionCN: 大量，如 a lot of time。

entries.definition: A large amount of something good, as in a wealth of detail.
entries.definitionCN: 大量美好的事物，如 a wealth of detail。

entries.definition: An extremely large supply of something.
entries.definitionCN: 极其丰富的供给。

normalIntro.en: The noun is the Latin idea of fullness standing on its own, before any suffix turns it into an adjective.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词就是拉丁语「满」这一概念独立站着的样子，还没被任何后缀变成形容词。

normal.en: Plenty is the bare noun of fullness, so it needs of before another noun: plenty of time, plenty of room.
normal.cn: plenty 是表示「满」的光杆名词，所以接另一个名词时要加 of：plenty of time、plenty of room。

normal.en: Plentiful adds -ful to the same noun, which is why the adjective and the noun look so alike.
normal.cn: plentiful 是在同一个名词后加 -ful，所以形容词与名词长得几乎一样。

normal.en: Years of plenty is the noun naming a whole period, not a single heap of goods.
normal.cn: years of plenty 是名词在指一整段时期，而不是一堆货物。

normal.en: In plenty drops the of and works as an adverbial phrase meaning in large amounts.
normal.cn: in plenty 去掉 of，作副词性短语，表示「大量地」。

normal.en: The informal adverb use, as in plenty hot, keeps the meaning enough while changing the word class.
normal.cn: plenty hot 这类非正式副词用法保留了「足够」的意思，只改变了词性。

abstract.en: A noun for fullness can describe a season, a table or a stretch of time, because abundance is always abundance of something.
abstract.cn: 表示「满」的名词能形容一季、一桌或一段时间，因为充足总是某样东西的充足。

abstract.en: Plenty does not measure; it says that counting is no longer necessary.
abstract.cn: plenty 不做计量，它说的是「已经不必再数了」。

abstract.en: The same root gives a noun for stores and an adjective for harvests, so grammar follows the difference between the heap and its quality.
abstract.cn: 同一个词根给出指库存的名词和指收成的形容词，语法正好对应「堆」与「性质」的差别。

examples.en: There is plenty of room for everyone.
examples.cn: 地方很宽裕，谁都坐得下。

examples.en: The old stories describe years of plenty followed by years of hunger.
examples.cn: 古老的故事里，富足的年份之后接着是饥饿的年份。

examples.en: The soup is plenty hot for me.
examples.cn: 这汤对我来说已经够烫了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑棱提」——粮食扑棱棱堆满仓，提到手软也提不完，就是 plenty。

root: 拉丁语 plenus（满的）→ plenitas（充足）→ 古法语 plente → 中古英语 plente → 现代英语 plenty。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a full supply; the noun then extends to a whole period of abundance, and the same form works informally as an adverb of degree.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「装得满满的供给」；名词由此扩展到整段富足时期，同一形式又非正式地充当程度副词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: barn doors open on grain piled into a small hill, too much to bother counting.
core.cn: 核心意象：粮仓门敞着，谷物堆成小山，多到懒得去数。

branches.en: a jar filled well above the recipe
branches.cn: 罐子装得远超配方所需

branches.en: a village eating well for a whole season
branches.cn: 全村整整一季吃得宽裕

branches.en: a coat warm enough without a scarf
branches.cn: 外套够暖，不必再围围巾

branches.en: a table with more dishes than guests
branches.cn: 菜比客人还多的一桌

branches.en: store rooms that stay full through winter
branches.cn: 整个冬天都满着的库房

intro.en: The noun keeps the Latin stem of fullness, and English adds a noun suffix plus two later relatives built on the same stem.
intro.cn: 这个名词保留了拉丁语表示「满」的词干，英语再加上一个名词后缀，以及两个由同一词干长出的同族词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 女士；贵妇人；夫人（头衔）；女主人
definition_en: a polite word for a woman; also a woman of high social rank, a title before a name, or the woman who runs a household
core_image: 宴会上一位女士端着茶盏，满座宾客起身让路
scene: 宴会上灯光明亮，主人起身迎向门口的客人。 Every gentleman stood up when the lady entered the room.
sceneCN: 这里是「女士」（第 1 个义项：对成年女性的礼貌称呼）；句意为这位女士走进房间时，每位先生都站了起来。可辨识画面：宴席、起身的宾客、门口的身影。

pos.zh: 女士；贵妇人；夫人；女主人

derivatives.zh: 由 lady 加后缀 -like（像……的）构成，义为「举止像贵妇的；优雅的」
由 lady 加 -ship（身份、地位）构成，用于尊称贵族妇女「夫人」
由 land 与 lady 复合，指出租房屋或经营客栈的女主人，义为「女房东」

senses.title: A polite word for a woman
senses.titleCN: 女士；对女性的礼貌称呼
senses.definition: a polite way of referring to or addressing an adult woman
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌地指称或称呼一位成年女性
senses.example: The lady at the front desk helped me find my room.
senses.exampleCN: 前台那位女士帮我找到了房间。
senses.why: The Old English word named the woman who ran the household, and courtesy kept it as a respectful label for any adult woman.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词原本指掌管一家的女主人，礼貌用法把它保留为对任何成年女性的尊称。

senses.title: The mistress of a household
senses.definition: the woman who owns or runs a house or an establishment
senses.definitionCN: 拥有或掌管一个家、一处场所的女性
senses.example: She was the lady of the house and everyone answered to her.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这家的女主人，人人都听她安排。
senses.why: Because the old compound meant the woman in charge of the bread, the authority inside a home survived as a meaning of its own.
senses.whyCN: 原词本指负责烤面包的女人，掌管一家的意味就作为独立义项留存了下来。

senses.title: A title placed before a name
senses.definition: the title used before the name of a woman of noble rank
senses.definitionCN: 用在贵族女性姓名之前的尊称
senses.example: Lady Mary opened the charity fair.
senses.exampleCN: 玛丽夫人为慈善集市揭幕。
senses.why: A title is a fossil of rank: the old word for a noble housewife became the fixed label for titled women.
senses.whyCN: 头衔是等级的化石：原本指贵族家女主人的词，固定成了贵族女性的称谓。

senses.title: A woman hired for a particular job
senses.definition: a woman employed to do a particular job, as in cleaning lady
senses.definitionCN: 受雇从事某项工作的女性，如保洁女工
senses.example: The cleaning lady comes every Friday morning.
senses.exampleCN: 保洁女工每周五上午来。
senses.why: When the word is attached to a job name, the old polite label simply marks that the worker is a woman.
senses.whyCN: 当它跟在职业名称后面时，这个旧的礼貌称呼只用来标明干这份活的是女性。

intro.en: Lady goes back to an Old English compound that literally meant bread-kneader, the woman who fed and therefore ran the household.
intro.cn: lady 可追到一个古英语复合词，字面意为「揉面包的人」，即养活全家、因而管着全家的女人。

items.en: Hlāf meant bread, the same Germanic word that became loaf in modern English.
items.cn: hlāf 意为面包，与今天的 loaf 同出一个日耳曼词。

items.en: Dīge meant a kneader or maker of dough, formed from a verb for kneading.
items.cn: dīge 意为揉面者、做面团的人，由表示揉面的动词构成。

items.en: Put together, hlǣfdige was the bread-kneader, the woman who fed the household and therefore ran it.
items.cn: 两者合成 hlǣfdige，本指揉面做面包的女人，她养活全家，也就管着全家。

items.en: Middle English shortened and softened the long compound into lady, already applied to noblewomen and to the Virgin Mary.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个长复合词缩短、软化，写作 lady，已用来指贵族女性与圣母。

items.en: Modern English uses lady as a polite term, a noble title and a word for women in particular jobs.
items.cn: 现代英语把 lady 用作礼貌称呼、贵族头衔，以及指从事特定工作的女性。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds and words that share the spelling or the lady element; the near-meaning group collects words for women and forms of address.
note.cn: 形近组收共用拼写或共用 lady 这一成分的复合词；近义组收表示女性与称呼的用词。

entries.definition: A small flying beetle with red or orange spotted wings.
entries.definitionCN: 一种红色或橙色带斑点的会飞的小甲虫；构词里用了 lady。

entries.definition: Behaving in a quiet, graceful way thought to suit a lady.
entries.definitionCN: 举止安静优雅、被认为合乎贵妇身份的。

entries.definition: A deep spoon with a long handle, used for serving soup.
entries.definitionCN: 舀汤用的长柄深勺；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A set of steps used for climbing up or down.
entries.definitionCN: 供上下攀爬的一串梯级；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: An adult female person, the plain word that lady politely replaces.
entries.definitionCN: 成年女性；lady 是对它的一种礼貌替代。

entries.definition: A polite form used to address a woman, especially a customer.
entries.definitionCN: 称呼女性的礼貌用语，尤用于顾客。

entries.definition: A polite word for a man, the male counterpart of lady.
entries.definitionCN: 对男性的礼貌称呼，与 lady 相对。

entries.definition: A title used before the name of an unmarried woman or girl.
entries.definitionCN: 用于未婚女性或女孩姓名前的称谓。

normalIntro.en: The word was built from bread and kneading, and its family keeps returning to the household, the title and the polite label.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由「面包」与「揉面」合成，同族词反复回到家庭、头衔与礼貌称呼。

normal.en: Hlāf is bread and dīge is kneader, so a lady was first the woman who kneaded bread for the household.
normal.cn: hlāf 是面包，dīge 是揉面的人，所以 lady 最初指为全家揉面做面包的女人。

normal.en: The long form hlǣfdige explains why lady shows no trace of bread today: the compound was worn down over centuries.
normal.cn: 古英语长词 hlǣfdige 说明今天看不出「面包」的原因：这个词组在几百年里被磨损缩短了。

normal.en: Lady has the plural ladies, because a y after a consonant turns into ies.
normal.cn: lady 的复数是 ladies，因为辅音后的 y 要变成 ies。

normal.en: Ladybird is a compound: a small beetle named after Our Lady, not a bird at all.
normal.cn: ladybird 是复合词：这种小甲虫的名字来自圣母，其实根本不是鸟。

normal.en: Ladies and gentlemen is a fixed order, so the ladies always come first in that phrase.
normal.cn: ladies and gentlemen 是固定顺序，短语里女士总排在前面。

abstract.en: A word that began with bread suggests that rank in a household was first measured by who fed it.
abstract.cn: 一个从面包开始的词说明，家里的地位最初是按谁来养活全家来衡量的。

abstract.en: Lady survives as politeness, which shows how a job title can soften into a form of respect.
abstract.cn: lady 作为礼貌用语活了下来，说明一个职务称呼可以软化成一种敬意。

abstract.en: Calling someone a lady is a small gift of dignity, so the word carries courtesy rather than description.
abstract.cn: 称某人为 lady 是送出一份体面，所以这个词带的是礼貌而不是描述。

examples.en: The lady at the front desk helped me find my room.
examples.cn: 前台那位女士帮我找到了房间。

examples.en: A young lady asked me for directions.
examples.cn: 一位年轻女士向我问路。

examples.en: The cleaning lady comes every Friday morning.
examples.cn: 保洁女工每周五上午来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累地」——她踩着高跟鞋走了一整天，累得只想找块地坐下；记住 lady 是女士。

root: 古英语 hlǣfdige，由 hlāf（面包）与 dīge（揉面者）合成，本指做面包的女主人，后来泛指女士与贵妇。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a woman in charge of a household; the senses then spread to a general polite term, a noble title and women in particular jobs.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是掌管一家的女性；义项由此扩展到泛指的礼貌称呼、贵族头衔以及从事特定工作的女性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a woman holding a fresh loaf while the household gathers around her.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位妇人手里捧着刚出炉的面包，全家围着她转。

branches.en: a woman greeting guests at a bright banquet
branches.cn: 宴会上向宾客致意的女士

branches.en: a housewife handing out the day's bread
branches.cn: 女主人分派当天的面包

branches.en: a titled name printed on an invitation
branches.cn: 请柬上印着的贵族头衔

branches.en: a worker mopping the office floor at dawn
branches.cn: 清晨在办公室拖地的女工

branches.en: a photograph of a woman standing in a doorway
branches.cn: 一张妇人站在门口的照片

intro.en: Old English bread, the old word for a kneader, and two modern suffixes all meet in this word.
intro.cn: 古英语的「面包」、表示揉面者的旧词，以及两个现代后缀，都汇聚在这个词里。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic in origin and has no reliable Latin cognate.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词源自日耳曼语，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.meaning: lady plus bird, a small spotted beetle
items.meaningCN: lady 与 bird 复合，指带斑点的甲虫

items.meaning: land plus lady, a woman who owns a rented house
items.meaningCN: land 与 lady 复合，指出租房屋的女主人

definition_zh: 杰出的；出色的；未付的；未完成的；显著的
definition_en: extremely good and clearly above the usual standard, still owed or not yet paid, not yet done or settled, or easily noticed because it stands out
core_image: 一排人站在同一条白线后面，只有一个人往前多迈了半步，肩膀露在外面
scene: 答辩结束后的教室里，评审把一份厚厚的报告翻到最后一页，抬头看了看站在讲台边的年轻人。 The committee gave her an award for outstanding research.
sceneCN: 这里的 outstanding 是「杰出的、出色的」（第 1 个义项：远高于一般水平）；句意为委员会因她出色的研究而给她颁奖。图中可辨识物件：厚报告、讲台、评审的笔。

pos.zh: 杰出的；未付的；未完成的；显著的

derivatives.zh: 由 outstanding 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「杰出地；显著地」
由 stand 与 out 复合、次序颠倒而成，义为「出众的人或物」

senses.title: Much better than others
senses.definition: extremely good and clearly above the usual standard, so that people notice and praise it
senses.definitionCN: 极好而明显高于一般水平，因而被人注意并称赞
senses.example: The committee gave her an award for outstanding research.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会因她出色的研究而给她颁奖。
senses.why: Outstanding is out plus standing: something that stands out from a row of others is seen first, and being seen first slowly turns into being admired.
senses.whyCN: outstanding 是 out 加 standing：在一排事物中「立在外面」的那一个最先被看见，而最先被看见就慢慢变成了被称赞。

senses.title: Still owed and not yet paid
senses.definition: of money or a bill, still owed to someone and not yet paid
senses.definitionCN: 指钱款或账单仍欠着别人、尚未付清
senses.example: The company has several outstanding debts.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司有几笔未偿债务。
senses.why: An unpaid debt is one that keeps standing there, unsettled, long after it should have been cleared, so the picture of standing out turns into standing open.
senses.whyCN: 一笔未付的债就是一直「立在那里」没有结清的账，本该了结却仍留在原处，于是「突出」的画面变成了「悬着未结」。

senses.title: Not yet done or settled
senses.definition: of work, problems or questions, not yet finished, answered or decided
senses.definitionCN: 指工作、问题或疑问尚未完成、回答或决定
senses.example: Two outstanding issues remain before the contract can be signed.
senses.exampleCN: 合同签署之前还有两个待解决的问题。
senses.why: Work that is finished leaves the desk; work still standing on it is the work not yet done, which is why the word covers pending tasks as well as unpaid money.
senses.whyCN: 做完的活会离开桌面，仍立在桌上的就是还没做完的活，所以这个词既能指待办的活儿，也能指没付的钱。

senses.title: Easily noticed, standing out clearly
senses.definition: clearly noticeable, especially as a feature of a thing, without any judgement of quality
senses.definitionCN: 明显引人注意，尤指某一事物的特征，并不含好坏评价
senses.example: The most outstanding feature of the design is its low roof.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计最突出的特点是它低矮的屋顶。
senses.why: Here the word keeps its literal picture: the part that stands out from the rest is the part the eye catches first, whether it is good, bad or merely different.
senses.whyCN: 这里保留的是字面画面：从其余部分里凸出来的那块，就是眼睛最先抓住的那块，不管它好、坏还是仅仅不同。

intro.en: Outstanding is out plus standing, first recorded in the sixteenth century for something that projects or stands clear; the senses of unpaid money and of excellence grew out of that physical picture.
intro.cn: outstanding 是 out 加 standing，十六世纪最早记录时指「凸出、立在外面」的东西；未付的款项与卓越这两个义项都从这个身体可感的画面长出来。

items.en: Standan meant to stand or to take up a position, and it is the source of the modern verb stand.
items.cn: standan 意为站立、占据一个位置，是现代动词 stand 的来源。

items.en: Standing named the act of standing and also a person's position or rank.
items.cn: standing 既指站立这个动作，也指一个人的位置或名次。

items.en: The compound outstanding was used for something that projects beyond a surface or stands clear of others.
items.cn: 复合词 outstanding 用来指超出某个表面、或在其他东西之外立着的事物。

items.en: The word widened in two directions: a debt still standing unpaid, and a person or work that stands above the rest.
items.cn: 这个词向两个方向扩展：一是仍「立着」未付的账，二是高出其余的人或作品。

items.en: Modern English uses it for excellence, for money not yet paid, for matters not yet settled, and for any feature that stands out.
items.cn: 现代英语用它表示卓越、尚未支付的钱、尚未了结的事，以及任何突出的特征。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on stand and out; the near-meaning group collects words for excellence and for matters not yet closed.
note.cn: 形近组收由 stand 与 out 构成的词；近义组收表示卓越、以及表示「尚未了结」的词。

entries.definition: In a way that is far better than usual.
entries.definitionCN: 以远胜平常的方式；杰出地。

entries.definition: A person or thing that is clearly the best of a group.
entries.definitionCN: 一群中明显最好的那个人或那件东西。

entries.definition: A person's rank or reputation, or permanent rather than temporary.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人的地位或声望，或指常设而非临时的。

entries.definition: To grasp the meaning of something.
entries.definitionCN: 领会某事物的意思。

entries.definition: Extremely good of its kind.
entries.definitionCN: 同类中极好的。

entries.definition: Far better than usual, so that it forms an exception.
entries.definitionCN: 远胜平常，因而成为例外。

entries.definition: Of money or work, not yet paid for.
entries.definitionCN: 指钱款或劳动尚未得到支付。

entries.definition: Waiting to be decided or finished.
entries.definitionCN: 等待决定或完成的。

normalIntro.en: Outstanding rests on the plain physical fact of standing clear of a row, so its hooks keep that picture while the meanings travel towards money and praise.
normalIntro.cn: outstanding 建立在「从一排中站出来」这个朴素的实体画面之上，记忆钩子保留这个画面，让词义向金钱与赞美两头走。

normal.en: Outstanding is out plus standing, so the spelling already carries the picture of one thing standing clear of the rest.
normal.cn: outstanding 是 out 加 standing，拼写本身已经带着「某物立在其余之外」的画面。

normal.en: The money sense keeps the same picture: a debt stands there until it is settled, so it stays outstanding.
normal.cn: 金钱义保留同一画面：一笔债在结清之前一直立在原处，所以它是未付的。

normal.en: Outstandingly adds -ly and describes how well something was done, never how much money is owed.
normal.cn: outstandingly 加了 -ly，形容一件事做得多好，从不指欠了多少钱。

normal.en: Standout turns the two parts round for a person or thing that is obviously the best in a group.
normal.cn: standout 把两部分调过来，指一群中明显最好的那个人或那件东西。

normal.en: The old verb outstand is no longer used in ordinary English, so the adjective does the work alone.
normal.cn: 古动词 outstand 在现代英语里已不再使用，这项工作只由形容词独自承担。

abstract.en: A word built from standing suggests that excellence is often a matter of visibility: whatever stands out is noticed first.
abstract.cn: 一个从「站立」造出的词说明：卓越常常是可见度的问题，凡是站出来的，总被最先看到。

abstract.en: The same adjective covers praise and debt, which reminds us that what stands out can be either an honour or an obligation.
abstract.cn: 同一个形容词兼指赞美与欠款，这提醒人：站出来的东西，既可能是荣誉，也可能是义务。

abstract.en: One word holds both the best work and the unpaid bill, because both are things that refuse to leave the desk.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时装下最好的成果与未付的账单，因为这两样都不肯离开桌面。

examples.en: The committee gave her an award for outstanding research.
examples.cn: 委员会因她出色的研究而给她颁奖。

examples.en: The company has several outstanding debts.
examples.cn: 这家公司有几笔未偿债务。

examples.en: The most outstanding feature of the design is its low roof.
examples.cn: 这个设计最突出的特点是它低矮的屋顶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥特斯坦丁」——奥特站在队伍外面，站得最显眼；记住 outstanding 是杰出的、未付的。

root: 由 out（向外）与 standing（站立）复合，一般认为十六世纪出现，字面为「立在外面、凸出来」，由此分指显眼与卓越，以及仍「立着」未结清的账与未办完的事；stand 属日耳曼语词，无可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one thing standing clear of a row; the senses divide into being admired for it, money still standing unpaid, work still standing unfinished, and a feature that simply stands out.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一样东西从一排之中站出来；义项按「因此被称赞」「钱仍立着未付」「活儿仍立着没完」「特征本身突出」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of people behind one white line, one of them half a step forward, a shoulder clear of the rest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排人站在同一条白线后面，只有一个人往前多迈了半步，肩膀露在外面。

branches.en: one report that the panel reads twice
branches.cn: 被评审读了两遍的那份报告

branches.en: a bill that stays on the desk for months
branches.cn: 在桌上压了几个月的账单

branches.en: two questions still waiting before a signature
branches.cn: 签字前仍悬着的两个问题

branches.en: a low roof that catches the eye at once
branches.cn: 一眼就抓住视线的低矮屋顶

branches.en: the same word for merit and for mere visibility
branches.cn: 同一个词，既指功绩，也指单纯的显眼

intro.en: The word joins a direction word to the old verb for standing, so its parts still say plainly: standing out of the line.
intro.cn: 这个词把方向词与表示站立的古老动词结合，各部分至今仍明白地说：站到队伍之外。

latinIntro.en: Outstanding is built from Old English standan and ūt, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this compound.
latinIntro.cn: outstanding 由古英语 standan 与 ūt 构成，这个复合词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: to be upright on the feet
forming a participle or a noun
a clearly superior person or thing

definition_zh: 决定；决心；裁决；判决
definition_en: a choice that you make after thinking
core_image: 天平静下来后指向的那一端
scene: 班会上大家举手表决春游地点。 Our decision was to visit the science museum this spring.
sceneCN: 这里 decision 是「决定」（第 1 个义项：思考后的选择）；句意是我们决定今年春天去科技馆。

derivatives.zh: decision 的动词形式，义为「决定」
由 decision 的词根加 -ive 构成，义为「果断的」
由 in-（不）加 decision 构成，义为「犹豫不决」

senses.title: A choice made after thinking
senses.definition: the choice you make after thinking about it
senses.definitionCN: 思考之后做出的选择
senses.example: Choosing my science project topic was a hard decision.
senses.exampleCN: 选科学课的研究题目是个艰难的决定。
senses.why: When the mind's scale settles, the settled side gets a name.
senses.whyCN: 心中的天平静下来之后，停下的一端需要名字，那便是决定。

senses.title: An official judgement
senses.definition: an official judgement made by a referee, court or judge
senses.definitionCN: 由裁判、法庭等做出的正式判断
senses.example: Everyone accepted the referee's decision calmly.
senses.exampleCN: 大家平静地接受了裁判的裁决。
senses.why: The court's scale settles not only one mind but the whole room.
senses.whyCN: 法庭或裁判的天平替全场人拨定方向，于是决定义延伸到正式裁决。

intro.en: Decision comes from Latin, the noun family of decide.
intro.cn: decision 来自拉丁语，是 decide 的名词家族。

items.en: Decisio meant a cutting off, the act of settling.
items.cn: 拉丁语 decisio 意为切下、了结。

items.en: Roman law used it for the act of judging a dispute.
items.cn: 罗马法用它指对争议的裁定行为。

items.en: Old French carried decision into writing.
items.cn: 古法语把 decision 带进书面语。

items.en: English took it in the fifteenth century, mostly in formal use.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪吸收 decision，多用于正式场合。

items.en: Everyday speech made it a common word for any choice.
items.cn: 现代英语的日常口语把它变成任何选择的常用词。

note.en: These words share the decide family or describe settled outcomes.
note.cn: 这些词属于 decide 词族，或描述已定的结果。

entries.definition: the verb of decision
entries.definitionCN: 决定（动词）

entries.definition: able to settle things
entries.definitionCN: 果断的

entries.definition: unable to choose
entries.definitionCN: 犹豫不决

entries.definition: separating into parts, different root
entries.definitionCN: 分开（拼写相近，词源无关）

entries.definition: crashing together, different root
entries.definitionCN: 碰撞（拼写相近，词源无关）

entries.definition: the thing you pick
entries.definitionCN: 选择

entries.definition: what you decide after thinking
entries.definitionCN: 结论

entries.definition: an official decision
entries.definitionCN: 裁定

entries.definition: a firm decision
entries.definitionCN: 决心；决议

entries.definition: an opinion or ruling
entries.definitionCN: 判断；裁决

normalIntro.en: Use the settled scale image and the decide family.
normalIntro.cn: 用「天平停稳」的画面和 decide 词族。

normal.en: decision is decide with a noun ending.
normal.cn: decision 是 decide 加名词后缀构成的。

normal.en: make a decision is the common phrase.
normal.cn: 常用短语是 make a decision（做决定）。

normal.en: indecision means no decision, just hesitating.
normal.cn: indecision 表示没有决定、只是犹豫。

normal.en: -sion words end with a zh or sh sound.
normal.cn: -sion 结尾的词发 /ʒ/ 或 /ʃ/ 音。

normal.en: a final decision ends all the talk.
normal.cn: a final decision（最终决定）终结所有讨论。

abstract.en: Picture a scale finally resting on one side.
abstract.cn: 想象天平终于停稳在一侧。

abstract.en: Hear the class cheering when the vote is announced.
abstract.cn: 听全班在表决结果宣布时的欢呼。

abstract.en: Feel your shoulders relax once the choice is made.
abstract.cn: 体会选定之后肩膀放松下来的感觉。

examples.en: After long talk, our decision was to plant trees by the river.
examples.cn: 长谈之后，我们决定在河边种树。

examples.en: The coach's decision to change players saved the game.
examples.cn: 教练换人的决定挽救了这场比赛。

examples.en: Writing down my decision helped me stop hesitating.
examples.cn: 把决定写下来帮我停止了犹豫。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「低遂心」——低声说「遂了心愿」，做出「决定」

root: 来自拉丁语 decisio（切下、了结），是 decidere（切掉多余选项）的名词形式；进入英语后泛指一切思考后的决定。

sensesIntro.en: Decision names the settled end of thinking, then official rulings.
sensesIntro.cn: decision 指思考停稳后的结果，再延伸到正式裁决。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the scale at rest
core.cn: 核心意象：停稳的天平

branches.en: The choice after thinking
branches.cn: 思考后的选择

branches.en: The ruling from officials
branches.cn: 官方的裁决

branches.en: Written plans start with a decision
branches.cn: 成文的计划始于决定

branches.en: Both end the waiting
branches.cn: 两者都终结等待

branches.en: Courts and referees give verdicts
branches.cn: 法庭与裁判给出裁定

intro.en: Decision keeps the Latin cutting root with a noun ending.
intro.cn: decision 保留拉丁「切」词根并加名词后缀。

latinIntro.en: The root cid or cis comes from caedere, to cut.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 cid/cis 来自 caedere（切）。

definition_zh: 携带；搬运；运送；支撑；传染（疾病）
definition_en: to hold something and take it from one place to another, or to support and transmit
core_image: 双手抱着行李，一步一步把重量挪过站台
scene: 搬新教室那天，同学们轮流把书箱抬上楼梯。 On moving day the students took turns to carry the book boxes upstairs.
sceneCN: 这里 carry 是「搬运；携带」（第 1 个义项：抱着或驮着从一处移到另一处）；句意为搬教室时轮流抬书箱。

derivatives.zh: 由 carry 加 -er 构成，义为「搬运工；带菌者；载体」
同根词，义为「四轮马车；车厢；运费」
同根词，义为「货物」

senses.title: To hold and move something
senses.definition: to hold a person or thing and take it to another place
senses.definitionCN: 抱、扛、提着人或物移往别处
senses.example: She carried her little brother on her back.
senses.exampleCN: 她背着小弟弟。
senses.why: Latin carricare meant to load a cart, and the cart's load became the verb's work.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 carricare 指给车装货，装车的活儿成了这个动词的职责。

senses.title: To support weight
senses.definition: to hold up the weight of a structure or person
senses.definitionCN: 撑住建筑或人的重量
senses.example: The bridge can carry heavy trucks.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥能承载重卡。
senses.why: A loaded cart rests on its wheels; supports too bear the load.
senses.whyCN: 装满的车压在轮上，支撑物同样负重。

senses.title: To take news, disease or sound along
senses.definition: to spread news, disease, electricity or sound from place to place
senses.definitionCN: 把消息、疾病、电流或声音带往各处
senses.example: Mosquitoes can carry malaria.
senses.exampleCN: 蚊子会传播疟疾。
senses.why: What a cart carries travels far, and so do news and germs in their own vehicles.
senses.whyCN: 车能载物远行，消息与病菌也各有自己的「车」。

senses.title: To keep on with an action
senses.definition: to put a plan or task into action, as in carry out
senses.definitionCN: 把计划或任务付诸实施，如 carry out
senses.example: They carried out the fire drill calmly.
senses.exampleCN: 他们冷静地完成了消防演习。
senses.why: A plan is like cargo: it must be loaded onto action and delivered.
senses.whyCN: 计划如货物，须装上「行动」并送达。

intro.en: Carry belongs to the great wheel family with car and cart.
intro.cn: carry 与 car、cart 同属「轮车」大词族。

items.en: Latin carrus meant a Gallic wagon, and carricare meant to load it.
items.cn: 拉丁语 carrus 指高卢双轮车，carricare 意为装车。

items.en: Northern Old French carier meant to transport by cart.
items.cn: 古法语北部方言 carier 意为用车运送。

items.en: Middle English carien kept both the load and the moving.
items.cn: 中古英语 carien 同时保留「装载」与「移动」。

items.en: Old Norse karfa, a bundle for carrying, mixed into the sense.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 karfa（背负的包裹）也汇入词义。

items.en: Modern carry spread to bridges, germs, plans and prices.
items.cn: 现代 carry 伸展到桥梁、病菌、计划与价格。

note.en: The first group collects wheel-and-load family; the second collects moving verbs.
note.cn: 第一组收「轮与载」词族，第二组收移动类动词。

entries.definition: A road vehicle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「汽车」，与 carry 同根。

entries.definition: Goods carried.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「货物」，同根。

entries.definition: A spiced dish, or to groom a horse.
entries.definitionCN: 名词/动词，义为「咖喱；刷马」，拼写相近但词源不同。

entries.definition: To move goods or people.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「运输」，正式用语。

entries.definition: To hold up; to endure.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承载；承受」，书面语。

entries.definition: To pull or drag heavily.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「拖运」，力感更强。

normalIntro.en: Remember carry inside the cart family.
normalIntro.cn: 在「车」词族里记 carry。

normal.en: carry comes from carricare, to load a cart.
normal.cn: carry 源自 carricare（装车）。

normal.en: car, cart and cargo are its cousins.
normal.cn: car、cart、cargo 是它的表亲。

normal.en: carry out means to put into action.
normal.cn: carry out 即执行。

normal.en: carry on means to keep going.
normal.cn: carry on 即继续。

normal.en: a carrier transmits things, even germs.
normal.cn: carrier 能载物，也能带菌。

abstract.en: Feel the box shift its weight into your arms.
abstract.cn: 想象箱子把重量压进双臂。

abstract.en: Hear breath quicken on the third flight of stairs.
abstract.cn: 三层楼后呼吸渐急。

abstract.en: See a relay runner pass the baton without stopping.
abstract.cn: 接力赛中棒不落地地交出去。

examples.en: The porter carried two suitcases at once.
examples.cn: 搬运工一次拎两只箱子。

examples.en: Flies can carry disease into the kitchen.
examples.cn: 苍蝇会把疾病带进厨房。

examples.en: We carried on with the match after the rain.
examples.cn: 雨后我们继续比赛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「凯利」——大力士凯利什么都扛得动。

root: 拉丁语 carrus（双轮车）→ carricare（装车）→ 古法语 carier → 英语 carry；同根词 car、cart、cargo、carriage、carrier。

sensesIntro.en: Carry grows from loading a cart to bearing weight, spreading news and germs, and finishing plans.
sensesIntro.cn: carry 从装车出发，长出承重、传播与执行诸义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a load that must get from here to there
core.cn: 核心意象：非从这里到那里不可的重负

branches.en: Things held and moved
branches.cn: 抱着搬着的东西

branches.en: Bridges and shoulders under weight
branches.cn: 承重的桥与肩膀

branches.en: News, germs and signals
branches.cn: 消息、病菌与信号

branches.en: Plans put into action
branches.cn: 付诸实施的计划

branches.en: Getting the job from start to end
branches.cn: 把活儿从起点送到终点

latinIntro.en: From carrus the family split into vehicles and into carrying.
latinIntro.cn: carrus 一分两支：一支成车名，一支成运词。

definition_zh: 座位；席位；使坐下；容纳
definition_en: a place to sit, a position in an organization, to place someone in a seat, or to have room for a number of people
core_image: 剧院里一排排红色座椅，灯光亮起，观众陆续入座
scene: 观众在开演前找到自己的座位。 The audience found their seats before the show.
sceneCN: 这里 seat 是「座位」（第 1 个义项）；句意：观众在开演前找到自己的座位。

derivatives.zh: 座位安排
坐着的
安全带
使下台；使落马

senses.title: A place to sit
senses.definition: a chair or place designed for someone to sit on
senses.definitionCN: 供人坐的椅子或位置
senses.example: Please take a seat.
senses.exampleCN: 请坐。
senses.why: The central sense is the physical place for sitting.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是供人坐的物理位置。

senses.title: A position in a group
senses.definition: a place as a member of a council, parliament, or company
senses.definitionCN: 在议会、委员会或公司中的成员位置
senses.example: She won a seat on the council.
senses.exampleCN: 她赢得了委员会的席位。
senses.why: A physical seat stands for the right to sit and vote.
senses.whyCN: 物理座位代指坐下与投票的权利。

senses.title: To place someone
senses.definition: to place someone in a seat
senses.definitionCN: 安排某人坐下
senses.example: The host seated us by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 主人安排我们坐在窗边。
senses.why: The noun becomes the action of placing someone.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为安排某人入座的动作。

senses.title: To have room for
senses.definition: to have enough seats for a number of people
senses.definitionCN: 有足够座位容纳一定人数
senses.example: The hall seats five hundred people.
senses.exampleCN: 这个大厅能容纳五百人。
senses.why: Counting seats becomes a way of stating capacity.
senses.whyCN: 计算座位成为说明容量的方式。

intro.en: Seat comes from Old Norse sæti, a sitting place, and is related to sit and to Latin sedere.
intro.cn: seat 源自古诺尔斯语 sæti（坐处），与 sit 及拉丁语 sedere（坐）同源。

items.en: Sæti meant a place to sit.
items.cn: sæti 意为坐处。

items.en: Related words named a dwelling or resting place.
items.cn: 相关词表示住所或休息之处。

items.en: Seat meant a chair or place for sitting.
items.cn: seat 意为椅子或坐处。

items.en: Seat came to mean a position in a governing body.
items.cn: seat 开始指在治理机构中的席位。

items.en: Seat also means to place someone or to hold an audience.
items.cn: 现代英语中 seat 还表示安排入座或容纳观众。

note.en: Seat is compared with similar short words and with words for furniture and places.
note.cn: 把 seat 与形近短词以及表示家具和位置的词作比较。

entries.definition: the salt water body

entries.definition: a sea animal, or a stamp
entries.definitionCN: 海豹；印章

entries.definition: to put something in place

entries.definition: a seat with a back

entries.definition: a long seat for several people

entries.definition: a particular position

normalIntro.en: Seat is the place, the position, and the act of sitting people down.
normalIntro.cn: seat 是座位、席位，也是安排人坐下的动作。

normal.en: Take a seat means sit down.
normal.cn: take a seat 意为坐下。

normal.en: A seat belt keeps you safe.
normal.cn: 安全带保护你。

normal.en: A seat in parliament is a political position.
normal.cn: 议会席位是一种政治职位。

normal.en: The host seats the guests.
normal.cn: 主人安排客人入座。

normal.en: A hall seats many people.
normal.cn: 大厅能容纳许多人。

abstract.en: A physical chair becomes a symbol of power.
abstract.cn: 一把实体椅子成为权力的象征。

abstract.en: To seat someone is to give them a place.
abstract.cn: 安排某人入座就是给他一个位置。

abstract.en: Capacity is measured by the number of seats.
abstract.cn: 容量以座位数量衡量。

examples.en: Please take a seat.
examples.cn: 请坐。

examples.en: She won a seat on the council.
examples.cn: 她赢得了委员会的席位。

examples.en: The hall seats five hundred people.
examples.cn: 这个大厅能容纳五百人。

dict_mnemonic.text: seat 与 sit 同源，核心是「坐的地方」；从座位引申出议会席位，再引申出「安排入座」与「容纳」。

root: 源自古诺尔斯语 sæti（坐处），与 sit 同源，核心义「供人坐下的位置」。

sensesIntro.en: Seat means a place to sit, a position in a group, to place someone, or to have room for people.
sensesIntro.cn: seat 意为座位、席位、安排入座，或容纳。

core.en: A place made for sitting.
core.cn: 为坐而设的位置。

branches.en: The physical chair or place.
branches.cn: 实体的椅子或位置。

branches.en: The right to sit and vote.
branches.cn: 坐下与投票的权利。

branches.en: Showing someone where to sit.
branches.cn: 安排某人坐在哪里。

branches.en: Having enough places for an audience.
branches.cn: 为观众提供足够座位。

branches.en: The place and the act of placing are linked.
branches.cn: 位置与安排入座的动作相互联系。

intro.en: Seat forms words for seating, safety, and removal from office.
intro.cn: seat 构成表示座位安排、安全与罢免的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin sedere, to sit, is a distant cognate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sedere（坐）是同源远亲。

items.meaning: a place to sit, or to place someone
sitting, or placed in a seat
a belt that holds a passenger
a person sitting next to you

definition_zh: 街区；居住区；邻里；附近；大约
definition_en: the area around where someone lives; the people living there; and, in fixed phrases, nearness in place or a rough amount
core_image: 一排低矮的房子围出一个小广场，孩子在三轮车旁追跑
scene: 街角的小店把长桌搬到门外，各家端来自己做的菜。 The whole neighbourhood turned out for the street party.
sceneCN: 这里 neighbourhood 是「街坊邻里」（第 2 个义项：住在这一带的人）；句意为整条街的街坊都出来参加街头聚会。图中可辨识物件：长桌、端菜的托盘、街角小店。

derivatives.zh: neighbourhood 的基础词，义为「邻居；毗邻」
由基础词 neighbour 加 -ing 构成，义为「邻近的；相邻的」
neighbourhood 的美式拼写，义为「街区；邻里」

senses.title: The area around one's home
senses.definition: the part of a town where someone lives, together with the streets and buildings around their home
senses.definitionCN: 一个人居住的那一片城区，包括住宅周围的街道与建筑
senses.example: She knows every shop in the neighbourhood.
senses.exampleCN: 这一带的每家店铺她都熟。
senses.why: The suffix -hood turns a neighbour into the state or range of neighbours, so the word starts as the zone marked out by people living near one another.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -hood 把 neighbour 变成「邻里所构成的状态或范围」，所以这个词最初就是由相互住得近的人划定的一片地带。

senses.title: The people who live in that area
senses.definition: the residents of such an area considered together as a community
senses.definitionCN: 把这一带的居民作为一个共同体来看
senses.example: The neighbourhood raised money for the new playground.
senses.exampleCN: 街坊们为建新游乐场凑了钱。
senses.why: Since the zone is named after the people inside it, the same word slides from the place to the people, a habit English often shows with words of community.
senses.whyCN: 既然这片地带是因住在里面的人而得名，同一个词就从地点滑到人身上，这是英语里表示共同体的词常见的走向。

senses.title: Nearness in place
senses.definition: the state of being close to a particular place, used in the fixed phrase in the neighbourhood of
senses.definitionCN: 靠近某一地点的状态，用于固定说法「在……附近」
senses.example: They bought a flat in the neighbourhood of the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在车站附近买了一套公寓。
senses.why: A neighbourhood is space around a point, so the word can serve in a purely spatial phrase that names no residents at all.
senses.whyCN: 街区本身就是某一点周围的空间，所以这个词能用在纯讲位置的短语里，完全不提住在那里的人。

senses.title: A rough amount or range
senses.definition: an approximate figure or amount, used in the phrase in the neighbourhood of
senses.definitionCN: 大致的数字或数量，用于短语「大约、上下」
senses.example: The repair will cost in the neighbourhood of three hundred pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 这次修理大约要花三百英镑。
senses.why: Approximation is spatial nearness moved onto numbers: a figure close to the target is treated as the value living nearby.
senses.whyCN: 近似就是把空间上的「靠近」挪到数字上：接近目标的数字，被当成住在旁边的那个值。

intro.en: Neighbourhood is neighbour plus the old suffix -hood, the same ending that builds childhood and brotherhood.
intro.cn: neighbourhood 是 neighbour 加上古老的词尾 -hood，与 childhood、brotherhood 用的是同一个词尾。

items.en: The suffix had meant condition, state or rank, and it became -hood in modern English.
items.cn: 词尾 hād 意为状况、状态或身份，在现代英语里变成 -hood。

items.en: The base word named the person who dwells near, as a compound of near and dweller.
items.cn: 基础词由「近」与「居住者」复合，指住得不远的人。

items.en: Middle English formed neighbourhood for the state of being neighbours and for the district where they lived.
items.cn: 中古英语构成 neighbourhood，既指互为邻居的关系，也指他们居住的地段。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the word is common for a district of a town and for the people in it.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，这个词已常用来指城里的一片地段以及住在里面的人。

items.en: Modern British English keeps neighbourhood and American English writes neighborhood, while the fixed phrase in the neighbourhood of extends the word to nearness and rough amounts.
items.cn: 现代英式保留 neighbourhood，美式写作 neighborhood；固定短语 in the neighbourhood of 又把词义扩到「附近」和「大约」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built with the same -hood suffix; the near-meaning group gathers words for districts and their people.
note.cn: 形近组收用同一个 -hood 词尾构成的词；近义组收表示地段及其居民的词。

entries.definition: The period of life when a person is a child.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人身为孩子的时期；童年。

entries.definition: The relationship between brothers, or a group united by a shared cause.
entries.definitionCN: 兄弟之间的关系，或为共同事业联合起来的团体。

entries.definition: The state of being untrue, or a statement that is untrue.
entries.definitionCN: 虚假的状态，或一句不实的话。

entries.definition: A defined part of a town or country.
entries.definitionCN: 城镇或国家中划定的区域。

entries.definition: The area near a particular place.
entries.definitionCN: 某一地点附近的区域。

entries.definition: The people of a particular area considered together.
entries.definitionCN: 把某一地区的人作为一个整体来看的群体。

normalIntro.en: The word is neighbour plus -hood, and the suffix does the same work it does in childhood: it turns a person into a state or a stretch of life.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 neighbour 加 -hood，词尾的作用与在 childhood 里一样：把人变成一种状态或一段生活。

normal.en: The suffix -hood comes from an Old English word for condition, so neighbourhood is the condition or zone of being neighbours.
normal.cn: -hood 出自古英语中表示「状况」的词，所以 neighbourhood 就是「互为邻居」的状况或范围。

normal.en: Childhood, brotherhood and neighbourhood all use the same ending, which is why they look and feel alike.
normal.cn: childhood、brotherhood、neighbourhood 用的是同一个词尾，所以它们看上去、读起来都很像。

normal.en: American English writes neighborhood, dropping the u that British English keeps.
normal.cn: 美式写作 neighborhood，去掉了英式保留的 u。

normal.en: The phrase 「in the neighbourhood of」 works for both a place and a number, so it means near as well as about.
normal.cn: 短语「in the neighbourhood of」既能接地点又能接数字，所以既表示「附近」也表示「大约」。

normal.en: Neighbourhood watch is a real arrangement in which residents keep an eye on one another's homes.
normal.cn: neighbourhood watch 是真实存在的做法，居民互相照看彼此的房子。

abstract.en: Adding -hood to a person makes a place, a quiet reminder that streets are made of the people standing on them.
abstract.cn: 给一个人加上 -hood 就得到一个地方，这悄悄提醒人：街道是由站在上面的人组成的。

abstract.en: One word can mean a district, its residents and an approximate sum, because all three are measured from the same centre.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能指一片地段、住在里面的人以及一个大致的数目，因为三者都从同一个中心量起。

abstract.en: A word that turns nearness into a number shows how easily English moves from space to quantity.
abstract.cn: 一个把「靠近」变成数字的词，说明英语从空间滑到数量有多容易。

examples.en: The whole neighbourhood came out for the street party.
examples.cn: 整条街的街坊都出来参加街头聚会。

examples.en: She has lived in this neighbourhood for thirty years.
examples.cn: 她在这个街区住了三十年。

examples.en: The cost will be in the neighbourhood of two hundred pounds.
examples.cn: 费用大约两百英镑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「邻里护」——街坊互相护着，就有了邻里情；记住 neighbourhood 是街区、邻里。

root: 古英语 neah（近）加 gebur（居住者）构成 neahgebur（邻居），再加 hād（状态，后作 -hood）构成 neighbourhood；美式拼写 neighborhood。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the zone made by people living near one another; it splits into the place, the people, and two phrases of nearness and approximation.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是由相互住得近的人围出的地带；它分成地点、居民，以及表示邻近与约数的两个短语义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small square of low houses with children racing between the doors.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈低矮的房子围出小广场，孩子在门与门之间追跑。

branches.en: a corner shop with its table moved onto the pavement
branches.cn: 把长桌搬到人行道上的街角小店

branches.en: neighbours bringing dishes to one long table
branches.cn: 街坊各自端菜到同一张长桌上

branches.en: a collection box passed from door to door
branches.cn: 挨家挨户传递的募捐盒

branches.en: a flat two streets from the station
branches.cn: 离车站两条街的一套公寓

branches.en: a repair bill rounded to a rough figure
branches.cn: 被估成整数的修理账单

intro.en: The word is built from the Old English compound for a person living near, plus the suffix -hood that turns a person into a state or an area.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语中表示「住得近的人」的复合词，加上把「人」变成状态或范围的词尾 -hood 构成。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and has no reliable Latin cognate; all of its parts are Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属于日耳曼语，没有可靠的拉丁同族词；它的构件全部来自古英语。

definition_zh: 蝙蝠；球棒；球拍；用棒击球
definition_en: a small animal that flies at night, or a wooden club used to hit a ball
core_image: 夜里一只蝙蝠擦着屋檐飞过，翅膀薄得像纸
scene: 傍晚的屋檐下，一只黑色的小动物贴着墙飞快掠过，几乎看不清。 A bat flew out of the old cave at dusk.
sceneCN: 这里 bat 是「蝙蝠」（第 1 个义项：会飞的哺乳动物）；句意为黄昏时一只蝙蝠从旧山洞里飞了出来。

pos.zh: 动词：用棒击球；轮到击球

derivatives.zh: 由 bat 加 -er 构成，义为「击球手」
由 bat 加 -ing 构成，义为「击球」
由 bat 加 -y 构成，义为「古怪的、发疯的」

senses.title: The flying animal
senses.definition: a small furry animal with wings that flies at night and rests upside down by day
senses.definitionCN: 白天倒挂休息、夜间飞行的小型毛茸茸动物，长有翼膜
senses.example: A bat flew out of the old cave at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时一只蝙蝠从旧山洞里飞了出来。
senses.why: The animal sense comes from an old word for this creature, which is unrelated to any club.
senses.whyCN: 动物义来自指这种动物的古词，与任何「棍棒」都没有关系。

senses.title: A club for hitting a ball
senses.definition: a specially shaped wooden or metal club used to hit a ball in games
senses.definitionCN: 比赛中用来击球的、形状特制的木制或金属棒
senses.example: He picked up the bat and walked to the plate.
senses.exampleCN: 他拿起球棒，走向击球位置。
senses.why: The club sense comes from a separate old word meaning a stick or a blow, and only the spelling is shared with the animal.
senses.whyCN: 「球棒」义来自另一个表示「棍子、击打」的古词，与动物义只是共用拼写而已。

senses.title: To hit with a bat
senses.definition: to hit a ball with a bat, or to take a turn at hitting
senses.definitionCN: 用球棒击球，或轮到上场击球
senses.example: She batted the ball far into the outfield.
senses.exampleCN: 她把球击到很远的外野。
senses.why: The verb is the club in action: swinging the stick so that it strikes the ball.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是那条球棒在动作：挥动棍子让它击中球。

intro.en: Bat is two different words with one spelling: the animal and the club each have their own history.
intro.cn: bat 是两个共用一个拼写的不同词：动物义与棍棒义各有自己的历史。

items.en: The animal word appears in Middle English in forms like bakke, and its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 动物义在中古英语中以 bakke 等形式出现，更早来源不确定。

items.en: Related forms for the animal occur in Scandinavian languages, which supports a northern source, though this is not settled.
items.cn: 斯堪的纳维亚诸语中有指这种动物的相关形式，支持北方来源，但尚未定论。

items.en: A separate word batt meant a stick or a blow, and it is the source of the club sense.
items.cn: 另有一个古英语词 bat，意为「棍子、击打」，是「球棒」义的来源。

items.en: The club word spread with bat-and-ball games, and the verb to bat followed the noun.
items.cn: 棍棒词随击球运动传播，动词 bat 则由名词而来。

items.en: The two words now look identical, and only the context tells you whether the animal or the club is meant.
items.cn: 两个词现在完全同形，只能靠上下文判断指的是动物还是球棒。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the club sense; the near-meaning group gathers the animal, the club, and the act of hitting.
note.cn: 形近组收由「棍棒」义构成的词；近义组收这种动物、球棒以及击球动作。

entries.definition: The player who hits with the bat, or a mixture beaten together in cooking.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「击球手」，也指烹饪中搅打成的面糊；由 bat 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: The act or turn of hitting the ball with a bat.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「击球」，由 bat 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: Informal adjective meaning slightly crazy, as if fluttering like a bat.
entries.definitionCN: 口语形容词，义为「古怪的、有点疯的」，像蝙蝠一样乱飞。

entries.definition: A thin stick used by a conductor or a runner; it comes from French and only looks similar.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「指挥棒、接力棒」；只是拼写相近，词源来自法语，与 bat 无关。

entries.definition: A heavy stick used to hit; broader and rougher than a bat.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「棍棒」，比球棒更粗更泛。

entries.definition: A bat with strings, used in tennis and badminton.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「球拍」，带网线，用于网球与羽毛球。

entries.definition: A night bird; like a bat it is active after dark, but it is a bird.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「猫头鹰」，也夜间活动，但属鸟类。

entries.definition: To move a bat or club through the air in order to hit.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「挥动」，指把球棒或棍棒挥向球。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two separate histories of the word, the suffixes -er, -ing, -y, and the fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用这个词两条分开的历史、后缀 -er、-ing、-y，以及固定搭配。

normal.en: The animal and the club are unrelated: one flies at night, the other hits a ball.
normal.cn: 动物与球棒互不相干：一个夜间飞行，一个击打球。

normal.en: A batter is the person holding the bat, formed with -er.
normal.cn: batter 是握着球棒的人，由 -er 构成。

normal.en: At bat means it is your turn to hit, a phrase from baseball.
normal.cn: at bat 意为轮到你击球，是棒球里的说法。

normal.en: Blind as a bat is unfair to bats, which find their way by sound.
normal.cn: blind as a bat 对蝙蝠并不公平，它们靠声音辨路。

normal.en: Bat the ball shows the verb: the stick moves, and the ball flies away.
normal.cn: bat the ball 显示动词用法：棍子一挥，球就飞走。

abstract.en: Picture a thin wing folding and unfolding in the dark: no feather, only skin.
abstract.cn: 想象夜色里一片薄翼一收一展：没有羽毛，只有皮膜。

abstract.en: Picture a smooth wooden club resting against the plate: heavy at the end, narrow at the grip.
abstract.cn: 想象一根光滑的木棒靠在击球区：末端粗，握处细。

abstract.en: One spelling holds a night animal and a day game, because English often lets old words collide.
abstract.cn: 一个拼写同时装着夜间动物与白昼运动，因为英语常让古老词撞在一起。

examples.en: A bat flew out of the old cave at dusk.
examples.cn: 黄昏时一只蝙蝠从旧山洞里飞了出来。

examples.en: He picked up the bat and walked to the plate.
examples.cn: 他拿起球棒，走向击球位置。

examples.en: She batted the ball far into the outfield.
examples.cn: 她把球击到很远的外野。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「巴特」——巴特夜里挥棒，棒子一挥惊起蝙蝠：蝙蝠、球棒

root: bat 有两条互不相关的来源：表示「蝙蝠」的词见于中古英语 bakke 等形式，更早来源不确定，斯堪的纳维亚诸语中有相关形式；表示「棍棒、击打」的 bat 来自古英语 bat，是「球棒」与动词「击球」的来源。两者现代同形。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of bat come from two separate words that share a spelling: the flying animal, the club, and the act of swinging that club.
sensesIntro.cn: bat 的三个义项来自两个共用同一拼写的不同词：会飞的动物、击球的棍棒，以及挥动那根棍棒的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin wing cuts through the evening air while a smooth wooden club waits on the ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片薄翼划过傍晚的空气，地上则静静靠着一根光滑的木棒。

branches.en: THE ANIMAL: one old word names the creature that flies after dark.
branches.cn: 动物线：一个古词指这种天黑后飞行的生物。

branches.en: THE CLUB: a different old word names the stick used to strike a ball.
branches.cn: 棍棒线：另一个古词指用来击球的棍子。

branches.en: THE ACT: the verb is the club swinging into the ball.
branches.cn: 动作线：动词就是球棒挥向球。

branches.en: THE NIGHT: the animal is tied to dusk, caves, and eaves.
branches.cn: 夜晚线：这种动物与黄昏、山洞、屋檐连在一起。

branches.en: THE GAME: the club and the swing exist for bat-and-ball sports.
branches.cn: 比赛线：球棒与挥击都是为击球运动而存在。

intro.en: Bat is a short root with two histories; English adds -er, -ing and -y to build its small family.
intro.cn: bat 是有两条历史的短词根，英语用 -er、-ing、-y 构成它的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Neither sense is Latin in origin and no Latin cognate is recorded, so the list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 两个义项都不源于拉丁语，也没有记录在案的拉丁同族词，因此列表留空。

items.exampleCN: 那只蝙蝠倒挂在屋顶下。

definition_zh: 吹；刮；吹奏；爆炸；（名词）打击
definition_en: to send air out or move air, to break apart with force, or a hard hit
core_image: 一口气吹灭生日蛋糕上的蜡烛
scene: 生日聚会上，孩子深吸一口气，吹灭了蛋糕上的蜡烛。 The child blew out the candles on the cake.
sceneCN: 这里 blow 是「吹」（第 1 个义项：把空气从嘴里送出去）；句意为孩子吹灭了蛋糕上的蜡烛。

derivatives.zh: 由 blow 加 -er 构成，义为「吹风机；鼓风机」
由 blow 与 out 组合而成，义为「爆胎；大获成功」
由 blow 与 up 组合而成，义为「爆炸；发火」
由 blow 加 -y 构成，义为「刮风的」

senses.title: To send out air
senses.definition: to send air out of the mouth, or to move air with force
senses.definitionCN: 把空气从口中送出，或用力量推动空气
senses.example: She blew on the hot soup.
senses.exampleCN: 她对着热汤吹气。
senses.why: Old English blawan meant to breathe out hard, and blowing out air is still the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 blawan 意为用力呼气，把空气吹出去仍是第一个义项。

senses.title: Of wind
senses.definition: used of the wind: to move strongly
senses.definitionCN: 用于风：强劲地移动
senses.example: The wind blew all night.
senses.exampleCN: 风刮了一整夜。
senses.why: The wind does the same thing a mouth does on a larger scale, so the verb serves both.
senses.whyCN: 风做的事和嘴做的事只是规模不同，所以同一个动词两处都管。

senses.title: To make a sound
senses.definition: to play a horn, whistle or other instrument by sending air through it
senses.definitionCN: 把空气送过号角、哨子或其他乐器来演奏
senses.example: He blew a whistle to stop the game.
senses.exampleCN: 他吹响哨子叫停了比赛。
senses.why: An instrument sounds when air is blown through it, so playing it is simply another blow.
senses.whyCN: 乐器因为空气被吹进去才发声，所以演奏不过是另一种「吹」。

senses.title: To burst apart
senses.definition: to break open or destroy something with an explosion
senses.definitionCN: 用爆炸使某物破裂或摧毁
senses.example: The storm blew down the old wall.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨把旧墙吹倒了。
senses.why: A blast of air or gas can tear a thing apart, so the word grew a sense of violent bursting.
senses.whyCN: 一股气体或气流能把东西撕裂，于是这个词长出了猛烈爆开的意思。

senses.title: A hard hit
senses.definition: a hard hit with the hand or a weapon, or a sudden bad event
senses.definitionCN: 用手或武器的一记重击，也指突如其来的坏事
senses.example: Losing the job was a heavy blow.
senses.exampleCN: 失去工作是沉重的打击。
senses.why: The noun first named a stroke or hit, and later any sharp misfortune that lands like one.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词最初指一记击打，后来泛指任何像一记重拳那样落下的不幸。

intro.en: Blow is an old verb of breathing and wind, and its noun branch grew a sense of hitting.
intro.cn: blow 是古老的「呼吸与风」动词，它的名词一支长出了「击打」的意思。

items.en: Old English blawan meant to blow, breathe out or puff, and it described both mouths and wind.
items.cn: 古英语 blawan 意为吹、呼气或喷气，既用于嘴也用于风。

items.en: German blähen and Dutch blazen are relatives, all built on a root for swelling and breathing.
items.cn: 德语 blähen 与荷兰语 blazen 是亲属词，都建立在表示「膨胀、呼吸」的词根上。

items.en: The verb kept the old strong forms blew and blown instead of adding -ed.
items.cn: 这个动词保留了古老的强变化形式 blew 与 blown，而没有加 -ed。

items.en: A separate noun blow, probably from a different root, meant a stroke or hit.
items.cn: 另有一个名词 blow，可能来自不同词根，表示一记击打。

items.en: Today the verb covers air, wind, music and explosions, while the noun means a hit or a shock.
items.cn: 今天这个动词覆盖吹气、刮风、吹奏与爆炸，名词则表示击打或打击。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words close in shape; the near-meaning group collects words for wind and hits.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写接近的词；近义组收与风、击打有关的词。

entries.definitionCN: 介词或副词，义为「在下面」，拼写与 blow 相近。

entries.definition: A deep round dish used for food.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「碗」，拼写与 blow 相近。

entries.definition: The colour of a clear sky.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「蓝色（的）」，与 blew 同音。

entries.definition: To blow out a short burst of air or smoke.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「喷出；吹出一口」。

entries.definition: A sudden strong rush of wind.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一阵狂风」，对应 blow 的风义。

entries.definition: To burst with great force and noise.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「爆炸」，对应 blow 的爆裂义。

entries.definition: A single movement of the hand or a weapon, a hit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一击」，对应 blow 的击打义。

normal.en: Old English blawan meant to breathe out hard, and it covered both mouths and wind.
normal.cn: 古英语 blawan 意为用力呼气，既用于嘴也用于风。

normal.en: The old strong forms blew and blown survive instead of a regular -ed ending.

normal.en: An instrument sounds because air is blown through it, so playing is another kind of blowing.

normal.en: It commonly pairs with out, up, away and whistle.

abstract.en: See a child puff out one breath and the candles go dark: that is blow.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子呼出一口气，蜡烛随之熄灭：那就是 blow。

abstract.en: Make the same breath a storm, and it can tear a wall down.
abstract.cn: 把同一口气放大成风暴，它就能把墙吹倒。

abstract.en: Say the word and let the candle smoke bring the sense back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让蜡烛的烟把意思带回来。

root: blow 来自古英语 blawan，意为吹、呼气或喷气，既用于嘴也用于风，德语 blähen 与荷兰语 blazen 是同源词。动词保留了古老的强变化形式 blew 与 blown。另有一个名词 blow，可能来自不同词根，表示一记击打，后来泛指任何像重击一样落下的不幸。今天动词覆盖吹气、刮风、吹奏与爆炸。

sensesIntro.en: All five senses of blow start from one picture: a burst of moving air, which can cool soup, drive wind, sound a horn, tear things apart, or land like a hit.
sensesIntro.cn: blow 的五个义项都从同一个画面出发：一股流动的空气，它能让汤变凉、推动风、吹响号角、撕裂物体，也能像一记重击那样落下。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one breath blowing out birthday candles
core.cn: 核心意象：一口气吹灭生日蜡烛

branches.en: THE BREATH: air sent from the mouth is the first and plainest sense.
branches.cn: 呼吸线：从嘴里送出的空气是最先也最朴素的义项。

branches.en: THE WIND: the same movement happens on a larger scale in the sky.
branches.cn: 风线：同样的运动在天空中以更大规模发生。

branches.en: THE SOUND: air through a horn or whistle turns blowing into music and signals.
branches.cn: 声音线：空气穿过号角或哨子，把「吹」变成音乐与信号。

branches.en: THE BURST: a strong blast can tear a thing apart.
branches.cn: 爆裂线：强劲的气流能把东西撕裂。

branches.en: THE HIT: the noun branch means a stroke, and then any sharp misfortune.
branches.cn: 击打线：名词一支表示一记击打，再引申为任何突然的不幸。

intro.en: Blow is a base verb and noun, so the items below are its endings, its strong forms and the words it joins.
intro.cn: blow 是基础动词兼名词，下面列出的是它的词尾、强变化形式以及与之组合的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin flare and sufflare are recorded words for blowing; they are parallels, not the source of blow.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 flare 与 sufflare 都是有记录的「吹」，它们是平行词，不是 blow 的来源。

items.example: Blawan is the recorded Old English source.
items.exampleCN: blawan 是有记录的古英语来源。

definition_zh: 礼貌地；客气地；委婉地；出于礼节地
definition_en: in a respectful and well-mannered way, especially when softening a refusal or following social form
core_image: 被磨圆的桌角，人从旁边走过不会被磕伤
scene: 面试结束时，年轻人起身把椅子推回原位，又向每位面试官点头道谢。 She politely thanked the interviewer and closed the door quietly behind her.
sceneCN: 这里是「礼貌地、客气地」（第 1 个义项：举止合乎礼节）；句意为她客气地道了谢，轻轻带上门离开。画面里有面试桌、推回原位的椅子和点头致意的年轻人。

derivatives.zh: 由 politely 去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到的形容词，义为「有礼貌的」
由 polite 加 -ness 构成，义为「礼貌；客气」
由否定前缀 im- 加 polite 构成，义为「无礼的」
由 impolite 加 -ly 构成，义为「无礼地」

senses.title: In a respectful, well-mannered way
senses.definition: in a way that shows respect for other people and follows the usual rules of good manners
senses.definitionCN: 以尊重他人、符合通常礼节规范的方式
senses.example: She politely introduced herself to every guest at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 她在门口客气地向每位客人做了自我介绍。
senses.why: The adjective descends from a Latin word for polished, so the adverb describes behaviour that has been smoothed down until it will not rub anyone the wrong way.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词来自拉丁语中表示「打磨过」的词，所以它形容的举止是被人磨平过的，不会硌到谁。

senses.title: In a way that softens a refusal
senses.definition: used when saying no or disagreeing in words chosen to avoid embarrassing the other person
senses.definitionCN: 在拒绝或表示不同意见时，用不使对方难堪的措辞
senses.example: He politely declined the offer and asked for more time.
senses.exampleCN: 他婉言谢绝了这个提议，请对方再给些时间。
senses.why: Once the word means smoothed manners, it is most useful exactly where friction is likely, so it clusters around refusals, complaints and disagreement.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词指的是被磨平的举止，它就最适合用在容易起摩擦的地方，于是总围着拒绝、抱怨与分歧打转。

senses.title: Out of social form rather than feeling
senses.definition: done because the situation requires courtesy, even when the feeling behind it is cold or absent
senses.definitionCN: 因为场合要求客气才这么做，背后的真实情绪可能是冷淡甚至没有
senses.example: The complaint was politely ignored for three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 那封投诉被客客气气地搁置了三个星期。
senses.why: Polish is surface work, so the adverb can mark the surface alone: the form is correct while nothing warm is happening underneath.
senses.whyCN: 打磨是表面功夫，所以这个副词可以只标记表面：形式无可挑剔，底下却没有一点热度。

intro.en: Politely is polite plus -ly, and polite goes back to a Latin verb meaning to polish, whose participle came to describe manners that had been smoothed.
intro.cn: politely 是 polite 加 -ly 构成的，而 polite 上溯到一个意为「打磨」的拉丁动词，其分词后来用来形容被磨平的举止。

items.en: Polire meant to polish or smooth a surface, and it was used of stone, wood and finished work.
items.cn: polire 意为打磨、使表面光滑，用于石头、木材与成品。

items.en: Its participle politus meant polished or refined, first of objects and then of anything carefully finished.
items.cn: 它的分词 politus 意为「被打磨过的、精致的」，先指物件，后指任何精心完成的东西。

items.en: In later learned Latin the same participle was applied to people, so a politus person was one whose manners had been smoothed.
items.cn: 在后来的学术拉丁语里，同一个分词被用到人身上，于是 politus 的人就是举止被磨平过的人。

items.en: English borrowed polite directly from Latin in the sixteenth century, and the adverb politely was formed by adding the native suffix -ly.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪直接从拉丁语借入 polite，副词 politely 则由加上本族后缀 -ly 构成。

items.en: Modern English uses politely for courteous speech, for tactful refusals, and sometimes for a courtesy that is only on the surface.
items.cn: 现代英语用 politely 表示客气的言辞、委婉的拒绝，有时也指只停留在表面的客气。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adjective and its relatives built on the Latin word for polished; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of courteous manner.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「打磨」一词上的形容词及其同族；近义组收表示「客气举止」的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective behind the adverb, meaning well-mannered.
entries.definitionCN: 副词背后的形容词，意为「有礼貌的」。

entries.definition: The quality of behaving courteously.
entries.definitionCN: 举止客气的品质；礼貌。

entries.definition: Rude or showing bad manners, formed with the negative prefix im-.
entries.definitionCN: 无礼的；缺少教养的，由否定前缀 im- 构成。

entries.definition: Rubbed until smooth, or done with great skill and care.
entries.definitionCN: 被磨得光滑的；也指做得极为精熟的。

entries.definition: In a way that shows formal good manners and respect.
entries.definitionCN: 以合乎正式礼节、表示尊重的方式。

entries.definition: In a way that shows regard for someone's position or feelings.
entries.definitionCN: 带着对他人地位或感受的敬重。

entries.definition: Politely but without warmth, the minimum of courtesy.
entries.definitionCN: 客气但不带热情，只到最低限度的礼貌。

entries.definition: In a way that avoids hurting or embarrassing people.
entries.definitionCN: 以不伤人、不使人难堪的方式。

normalIntro.en: The adverb is the Latin idea of polishing turned into a manner: smoothness applied to the way people treat each other.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词是拉丁语「打磨」这一概念转成举止：把光滑用在人与人相待的方式上。

normal.en: Politely is polite plus -ly, so it answers the question of how someone spoke or behaved.
normal.cn: politely 是 polite 加 -ly，回答的是「某人如何说话、如何行事」。

normal.en: The Latin source polire means to polish, which is why politeness is pictured as a surface made smooth.
normal.cn: 拉丁语来源 polire 意为打磨，所以「礼貌」被想成被打磨光滑的表面。

normal.en: Politely decline and politely refuse are the most common patterns, because the word is needed where a no must be softened.
normal.cn: politely decline 与 politely refuse 是最常见的搭配，因为这个词正用在必须把「不」说软的地方。

normal.en: The negative is impolite, with im- before p, not unpolite in ordinary modern use.
normal.cn: 否定形式是 impolite，在 p 前用 im-，现代常用语里不说 unpolite。

normal.en: Politeness is the noun and impolitely the negative adverb, so the family covers the quality, the manner and its lack.
normal.cn: politeness 是名词，impolitely 是否定副词，这一族词因此覆盖品质、方式与两者的缺失。

abstract.en: A word borrowed from polishing suggests that manners are not Nature but work done on a rough edge.
abstract.cn: 一个从「打磨」借来的词说明：礼貌不是天性，而是在粗糙的边上做的功夫。

abstract.en: Politely can be warm or cold, because smoothness says nothing about what is underneath.
abstract.cn: politely 可以是暖的也可以是冷的，因为光滑并不说明底下是什么。

abstract.en: The most useful courtesy appears exactly where people must say no to each other.
abstract.cn: 最有用的客气，恰好出现在人们必须彼此说不的时候。

examples.en: She politely introduced herself to every guest at the door.
examples.cn: 她在门口客气地向每位客人做了自我介绍。

examples.en: He politely declined the offer and asked for more time.
examples.cn: 他婉言谢绝了这个提议，请对方再给些时间。

examples.en: The complaint was politely ignored for three weeks.
examples.cn: 那封投诉被客客气气地搁置了三个星期。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坡莱特利」——把棱角磨平，把话说得体贴，人就显得客气，这就是 politely。

root: 拉丁语 polire（打磨）→ politus（被打磨过的、精致的）→ 中世纪拉丁语引申为「举止有礼的」→ 英语 polite，加 -ly 成 politely。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is smoothed behaviour; from it come the softened refusal and the courtesy that is only form.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「被磨平的举止」；由此分出委婉的拒绝，以及只停留在形式上的客气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a corner sanded round, so people can pass without being cut.
core.cn: 核心意象：被磨圆的一角，两个人擦身而过却不会互相割伤。

branches.en: a guest greeted by name at the door
branches.cn: 在门口被叫出名字问候的客人

branches.en: a head shaken gently with a smile
branches.cn: 带着笑轻轻摇头

branches.en: a letter answered with perfect but cold wording
branches.cn: 用挑不出错却冷淡的措辞回信

branches.en: a host easing a guest out without hurry
branches.cn: 主人不急不催地把客人送走

branches.en: a rejection that leaves no one embarrassed
branches.cn: 不叫任何人难堪的拒绝

intro.en: A Latin verb of polishing, its participle of refinement, and the English suffix -ly hold this adverb together, with -ness and im- building the noun and the negative.
intro.cn: 一个表示打磨的拉丁动词、它表示精致的分词，以及英语后缀 -ly，共同撑起这个副词；-ness 与 im- 再分别造出名词与否定形式。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

senses.example: He added two spoons of sugar to his tea.

senses.example: The body turns sugars into energy.

intro.en: Sugar travelled into English through Mediterranean trade words.
intro.cn: sugar 经由地中海贸易中的词汇传入英语。

items.cn: succarum 指这种甜味物质。

note.en: Sugar is compared with look-alike words and with words for sweeteners.

entries.definition: a thick sweet liquid
entries.definitionCN: 糖浆

entries.definition: a sweet food made by bees

normalIntro.en: Sugar is sweetness you can see as small crystals.
normalIntro.cn: sugar 就是能看见的一粒粒小晶体般的甜。

normal.en: He added two spoons of sugar to his tea.
normal.cn: 他在茶里加了两勺糖。

normal.en: The shop sells brown sugar and honey.
normal.cn: 这家店卖红糖和蜂蜜。

normal.en: Too much sugar is bad for the teeth.

normal.en: The body turns sugars into energy.

abstract.en: Sugar teaches us that small grains can change a whole cup.
abstract.cn: 糖告诉我们，小小的颗粒也能改变一整杯。

abstract.en: Sweetness is best measured by how little is needed.
abstract.cn: 甜味的最好衡量方式，是看需要多少才够。

abstract.en: What tastes sweet today may cost us tomorrow.
abstract.cn: 今天尝起来甜的，明天可能要付出代价。

examples.en: He added two spoons of sugar to his tea.
examples.cn: 他在茶里加了两勺糖。

branches.en: Blood sugar must stay balanced.

intro.en: Sugar builds sugary, sugared, and sugarless.
intro.cn: sugar 可构成 sugary、sugared 和 sugarless。

latinIntro.cn: 这个词根来自中世纪拉丁语 succarum。
