definition_zh: 人；人类的；人性的；有人情味的
definition_en: a person, or connected with people rather than animals, machines or gods
core_image: 一面既映出神也映出兽的镜子：中间站着的那个会哭会笑的影像
scene: 博物馆的玻璃柜里摆着古人类复原的头骨模型。 Human bones were found deep in the cave.
sceneCN: 这里 human 是形容词「人类的」（第 1 个义项：与人类相关）；洞穴深处发现了人骨。

pos.zh: 人的；人类的；有人情味的

derivatives.zh: human + -ity → 人类；人性；仁慈
同源词 → 仁慈的；人道的（拼法接近 human）
human + -ly → 在人力所及的范围内
in-（非）+ human → 无人性的；残忍的

senses.title: Connected with people, not animals or machines
senses.definition: belonging to people, their bodies, minds and society
senses.definitionCN: 属于人及人的身体、心智与社会
senses.example: Reading and writing are special human skills.
senses.exampleCN: 读写是人类特有的技能。
senses.why: The core sense draws a border: on one side animals and machines, on this side people.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是划界：一边是动物与机器，这一边是人。

senses.title: A person (noun)
senses.definition: a member of the human race; a person
senses.definitionCN: 人类的一员；一个人
senses.example: The rescuers found one last human under the fallen roof.
senses.exampleCN: 救援人员在倒塌的屋顶下找到了最后一个人。
senses.why: The adjective steps forward as a noun: the belonging itself names the member.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转为名词：归属本身成了成员的名字。

senses.title: Showing weakness and feeling typical of people
senses.titleCN: 有人性弱点的；有人情味的
senses.definition: showing the feelings, mistakes and kindness that people naturally have
senses.definitionCN: 流露出人类自然的情感、过失与善意
senses.example: Even great teachers are human and sometimes forget things.
senses.exampleCN: 再了不起的老师也是人，偶尔也会忘事。
senses.why: The border cuts both ways: to be human is also to err and to care.
senses.whyCN: 这条边界是双向的：作为人，既会犯错，也会体谅。

intro.en: Human comes from Latin humanus, of man, related to homo, a human being, and humus, the ground.
intro.cn: human 来自拉丁 humanus「人的」，与 homo「人」相关，而 homo 又与 humus「泥土」相关联。

items.en: Latin homo meant a human being; the old story links it to humus, the soil from which people were shaped.
items.cn: 拉丁 homo 指人；旧说把它与 humus（泥土）相连，因为人由泥土塑成。

items.en: The adjective humanus meant of man, cultured and kind; it built humanitas, learning and kindness.
items.cn: 形容词 humanus 意为「人的；文明的；仁慈的」，派生 humanitas「人文与仁慈」。

items.en: Old French humain carried the word into medieval English writing.
items.cn: 古法语 humain 把该词带入中世纪英语文本。

items.en: Middle English spelled it humain or humayne; the adjective came first.
items.cn: 中古英语拼作 humain 或 humayne，形容词用法先行。

items.en: Modern English added human being, human rights and the noun human.
items.cn: 现代英语造出 human being、human rights，并使 human 兼作名词。

note.en: Group one keeps the Latin family; group two keeps words about people and kindness.
note.cn: 第一组是拉丁词族；第二组是关于人与仁慈的近义词。

entries.definition: kind and merciful to people and animals
entries.definitionCN: 同源词，义为「仁慈的；人道的」

entries.definition: people as a whole; kindness; the humanities
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「人类；仁慈；人文学科」

entries.definition: cruel; without human feeling
entries.definitionCN: 同根反义词，义为「残忍的；无人性的」

entries.definition: a human being considered as an individual
entries.definitionCN: 个人，指一个个具体的人

entries.definition: all human beings together
entries.definitionCN: 人类整体，范围最大的说法

entries.definition: educated and behaving in a fair, ordered way
entries.definitionCN: 开化的；文明的，强调教养与秩序

normalIntro.en: Use the Latin soil story and the family.
normalIntro.cn: 用「泥土造人」的拉丁词源故事与词族记 human。

normal.en: human comes from humus, the soil: people shaped from the ground
normal.cn: human 来自 humus（泥土）：古人相信人由泥土塑成。

normal.en: humane looks like human but means kind and merciful
normal.cn: humane 与 human 形近，意思是「仁慈的」。

normal.en: human + -ity = humanity, people as a whole and kindness
normal.cn: human + -ity＝humanity：人类整体，也是仁慈。

normal.en: in + human = inhuman, without human feeling
normal.cn: in- + human＝inhuman，没有人的感情＝残忍的。

normal.en: a human error means a mistake made by a person
normal.cn: a human error＝人犯的错误＝人为失误。

abstract.en: Picture clay under a sculptor’s hand slowly taking a face.
abstract.cn: 想象雕塑家掌下的泥慢慢显出一张脸——泥土造人。

abstract.en: Picture a mirror showing a lion on one side and an angel on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一面镜子：一侧映出狮，一侧映出天使，中间站着人。

abstract.en: Feel the word as a handshake between two strangers.
abstract.cn: 把这个词感受成两个陌生人之间的握手——人情味。

examples.en: Only a human can feel sorry for a mistake like this.
examples.cn: 只有人会对这样的错误感到内疚。

examples.en: The robot imitated a human voice almost perfectly.
examples.cn: 机器人几乎完美地模仿了人声。

examples.en: Helping strangers is part of human nature.
examples.cn: 帮助陌生人是人性的一部分。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「休门」——歇了工的人从家门里走出来，一个活生生的人，就是 human（人）。

root: human 来自拉丁 humanus「人的；文明的」，词根 homo「人」旧说与 humus「泥土」相关（人由泥土塑成）；同根词有 humane、humanity、inhuman。

sensesIntro.en: Human first draws the line around people, then names one person, then softens into kindness and error.
sensesIntro.cn: human 先为人类划界，再指单个的人，最后落回人情的柔软与人的过失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the figure standing between god and beast
core.cn: 核心意象：站在神与兽之间的身影

branches.en: the line around the species
branches.cn: 围出物种边界的线（义项 01）

branches.en: one member named by belonging
branches.cn: 以归属命名的个体（义项 02）

branches.en: the soft side: error and kindness
branches.cn: 柔软的一面：过失与善意（义项 03）

branches.en: the class and its member share one word
branches.cn: 类与成员共用一词（义项 01 · 02）

branches.en: human rights protect the weak side
branches.cn: 人权守护柔软的一面（义项 03）

intro.en: Human heads a rich Latin family of people, kindness and culture.
intro.cn: human 是拉丁「人」词族的首领，涵盖人类、仁慈与文明。

latinIntro.en: Latin homo, hominis and humanus are the ancestors; homo also builds homicide and hominid.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 homo, hominis 与 humanus 是其祖先；homo 还派生 homicide 与 hominid。

items.example: a human voice on the phone

items.exampleCN: Homo sapiens 是我们物种的学名。
一个善待动物的人道协会

items.meaning: a member of the human family of species
items.exampleCN: 人科动物很早就直立行走。

definition_zh: 它自己；自身；（用于强调）本身
definition_en: used to show that a thing is the same one already mentioned, or to give emphasis to that thing
core_image: 镜子立在一件物体前，镜内镜外是同一样东西
scene: 孩子第一次看到镜中的自己，伸手去摸，镜子发出轻轻的一声响。 The old machine started itself after the power came back.
sceneCN: 这里 itself 是「它自己」（第 1 个义项：指同一个事物，动作回到自身），句意为来电后那台旧机器自己启动了。画面里的物件：镜子、控制面板、指示灯。

pos.zh: 代词：它自己；自身；（加强语气）本身

derivatives.zh: itself 的基础代词，义为「它」
由 it 加 s 构成，义为「它的」
itself 的组成部分，义为「自身」

senses.title: The same thing acts
senses.definition: used when the thing already mentioned is the one doing or receiving the action
senses.definitionCN: 当已提到的事物本身是动作的发出者或承受者时使用
senses.example: The door closed itself in the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 门被风吹得自己关上了。
senses.why: Self turns the pronoun back on its own subject, so the actor and the object are one.
senses.whyCN: self 把代词折回到主语身上，于是施动者和受动者是同一个。

senses.title: Emphasis on a thing
senses.definition: used to stress that this thing, and not another, is meant
senses.definitionCN: 强调所指正是这件东西而不是别的
senses.example: The building itself is old, but the inside is new.
senses.exampleCN: 这座建筑本身很旧，里面却是新的。
senses.why: Emphatic use points at the thing bare, as if removing everything around it.
senses.whyCN: 强调用法直指那件东西本身，仿佛把周围都去掉了。

senses.title: Acting without help
senses.definition: used with by to show that nobody else was involved
senses.definitionCN: 与 by 连用，表示没有别人参与
senses.example: The child can dress itself now.
senses.exampleCN: 这孩子现在能自己穿衣服了。
senses.why: By itself pushes the self-image to its limit: no helper is in the picture.
senses.whyCN: by itself 把「自己」推到极限：画面里没有任何帮手。

senses.title: Being the essence
senses.definition: used with in to say what something is when considered alone
senses.definitionCN: 与 in 连用，表示单看它本身的性质
senses.example: The offer is not bad in itself, but the timing is wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 这个提议本身不坏，只是时机不对。
senses.why: In itself takes the thing out of its context and looks at it alone.
senses.whyCN: in itself 把这件东西从情境里拿出来单独看。

senses.title: Returning to a state
senses.definition: used to say that a thing or person has come back to its normal state
senses.definitionCN: 表示某物或某人回到了常态
senses.example: The market slowly righted itself after the shock.
senses.exampleCN: 市场在冲击之后慢慢恢复过来。
senses.why: Something that rights itself has folded back to where it began.
senses.whyCN: 能一下扶正自己的东西，是折回了原来的位置。

intro.en: Itself is a compound made in English from it and self, after the pattern of himself and herself.
intro.cn: itself 是英语内部用 it 与 self 复合而成，模仿了 himself 与 herself 的模式。

items.en: Self was a separate noun and adjective for the same very person.
items.cn: self 原来自成名词和形容词，表示「正是本人」。

items.en: The pronoun was hit, so the compound shape came later.
items.cn: 当时的代词是 hit，所以这种复合形式出现较晚。

items.en: Reflexive forms such as himself and herself were already common.
items.cn: 反身形式如 himself、herself 已很常见。

items.en: Itself appeared as it replaced hit in ordinary speech.
items.cn: it 取代 hit 之后，itself 才出现。

items.en: The by itself and in itself phrases fixed in modern usage.
items.cn: by itself 与 in itself 这些说法在现代用法里固定下来。

note.en: The look-alike group is the it- family with self; the near-meaning group holds other reflexive pronouns.
note.cn: 形近组是 it 加 self 的词族；近义组收其他反身代词。

entries.definition: Belonging to it.
entries.definitionCN: 所有格形式，义为「它的」，与本词只差 self。

entries.definition: The pronoun for a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 基础代词，义为「它」，是本词的前半。

entries.definition: A person's own nature or body.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「自身」，是本词的后半。

entries.definition: Those same things or people, as a plural.
entries.definitionCN: 反身代词，义为「它们自己」，用于复数。

entries.definition: That same male person.
entries.definitionCN: 反身代词，义为「他自己」，itself 的模仿对象。

entries.definition: That same female person.
entries.definitionCN: 反身代词，义为「她自己」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the mirror image and the three fixed phrases by itself, in itself, and for itself.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用镜子画面，以及 by itself、in itself、for itself 三个固定说法。

normal.en: Itself is it plus self, like himself and herself.
normal.cn: itself 就是 it 加 self，与 himself、herself 同构。

normal.en: Self was once a separate word for the very person.
normal.cn: self 原先是表示「正是本人」的独立词。

normal.en: By itself means with nobody's help.
normal.cn: by itself 意为没有别人帮忙。

normal.en: In itself means considered alone.
normal.cn: in itself 意为单看它本身。

normal.en: Reflexive forms appeared after it replaced hit.
normal.cn: 反身形式是在 it 取代 hit 之后才有的。

abstract.en: Itself is a mirror in front of the thing.
abstract.cn: itself 就是立在那东西面前的一面镜子。

abstract.en: The machine that starts itself needs no hand.
abstract.cn: 会自己启动的机器不需要人的手。

abstract.en: What is old in itself may still be new inside.
abstract.cn: 本身很旧的东西，里面仍可能是新的。

examples.en: The problem will not solve itself.
examples.cn: 这个问题不会自己解决。

examples.en: The house itself is small, but the garden is huge.
examples.cn: 房子本身不大，但花园很大。

examples.en: The lamp switches itself off at midnight.
examples.cn: 这盏灯到午夜会自动关掉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一特塞奥夫」—— 一件东西特意把自己塞回自己身边

root: 古英语 self「本人；自身」（独立词）→ 中古英语 himself、herself 等反身形式 → 现代英语 it 加 self 构成 itself。同族有 it、its、self。

sensesIntro.en: Five uses: the same thing acting, emphatic itself, acting alone, considered in essence, and returning to a normal state.
sensesIntro.cn: 五种用法：同一事物自身施动、强调本身、独自行动、本质上如何，以及恢复常态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mirror standing before an object, identical inside and out.
core.cn: 核心意象：镜子立在物体前，镜内镜外一样。

branches.en: THE DOOR: the wind pushes it into itself.
branches.cn: 门这条线：风把它推回自己身上。

branches.en: THE BUILDING: old walls, new rooms.
branches.cn: 建筑这条线：旧墙与新房间。

branches.en: THE CHILD: buttons done without help.
branches.cn: 孩子这条线：不用人帮就扣上的扣子。

branches.en: THE OFFER: fair alone, wrong in timing.
branches.cn: 提议这条线：单看公道，时机不对。

branches.en: THE MARKET: shaken, then levelled again.
branches.cn: 市场这条线：震惊之后又回到原位。

intro.en: Itself joins two old English pieces, the pronoun it and the word self.
intro.cn: itself 把两块老英语成分拼在一起：代词 it 与 self。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source; the nearest Latin pattern is the reflexive suus, listed only for contrast.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁语来源，最接近的拉丁模式是反身词 suus，只作对照。

items.example: The possessive built on the same stem.
Kept as one word, never split.
items.exampleCN: 始终写成一个词，不拆开。

definition_zh: 神秘的；难以解释的；讳莫如深的
definition_en: strange and difficult to explain; having a hidden or supernatural quality; deliberately keeping things unclear
core_image: 一扇只开一条缝的门，缝里透出一点看不清的光
scene: 村口的老宅多年无人居住，夜里楼上的窗子却总亮着。 The old house keeps a mysterious light burning in its upper window.
sceneCN: 这里是「神秘的、难以解释的」（第 1 个义项：来路不明、说不清楚）；句意为那座老宅楼上窗里始终亮着一盏莫名的灯。图中可辨识物件：老宅、亮着的窗、夜色。

pos.zh: 神秘的；难以解释的；讳莫如深的

derivatives.zh: 由 mysterious 加 -ly 构成，义为「神秘地」
由 mysterious 加 -ness 构成，义为「神秘性」
与 mysterious 同出希腊语词根，义为「谜；神秘事物」

senses.title: Strange and hard to explain
senses.definition: difficult to understand or explain because the facts are hidden
senses.definitionCN: 因事实被遮蔽而难以理解或解释
senses.example: The old house keeps a mysterious light burning in its upper window.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老宅楼上窗里始终亮着一盏莫名的灯。
senses.why: Greek myein meant to close the lips or the eyes, so the family of words starts from what is shut away from view and only later describes how such a thing feels.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 myein 意为闭口或闭眼，因此这一族词的起点是「被关在视线之外的东西」，之后才用来形容这种东西给人的感觉。

senses.title: Touching on hidden or supernatural power
senses.titleCN: 带有神秘力量的；玄秘的
senses.definition: having a quality that seems to come from a hidden or supernatural source
senses.definitionCN: 带有似乎来自隐秘或超自然来源的性质
senses.example: The valley was said to hold mysterious forces that spoiled milk overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 据说那条山谷里有神秘的力量，能让牛奶一夜之间变坏。
senses.why: The word first named secret religious rites open only to the initiated; that closed door of ritual left it with a permanent air of the beyond.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指名只有入会者才能参加的秘仪；仪式那扇关着的门，让它永久带上了一层超验的气息。

senses.title: Deliberately unclear about something
senses.titleCN: 讳莫如深的；故意不说清
senses.definition: choosing to keep one's actions or intentions vague on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 有意把自己的行为或意图说得含糊
senses.example: She was mysterious about where the money had come from.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这笔钱的来路讳莫如深。
senses.why: Anyone who refuses to explain looks, from outside, exactly like a thing that cannot be explained, so the adjective moves from the unknown object to the person hiding it.
senses.whyCN: 一个人拒绝解释，从外面看就和一件无法解释的东西一模一样，于是这个形容词从被未知的对象转到了藏起它的人身上。

intro.en: Mysterious comes through French from Latin, where the noun had already travelled from Greek rites closed to outsiders.
intro.cn: mysterious 经法语来自拉丁语，而拉丁语中那个名词早已从「不许外人参与的希腊仪式」一路传来。

items.en: The verb myein meant to close, especially the eyes or the lips, and it gave the family its sense of shutting away.
items.cn: 动词 myein 意为闭合，尤指闭眼或闭嘴，为这一族词提供了「关起来、不示人」的意思。

items.en: A mysterion was a secret rite or doctrine revealed only to those admitted to it.
items.cn: mysterion 指只向获准入会者揭示的秘密仪式或教义。

items.en: Latin took the word as mysterium, keeping both the ritual sense and the broader sense of a secret.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个词写作 mysterium，既保留仪式义，也泛指秘密。

items.en: French formed the adjective mysterieux from the same stem, and it carried the sense of something unexplained rather than something sacred.
items.cn: 法语用同一词干造出形容词 mysterieux，词义已偏向「说不清的事」，不再限于神圣之事。

items.en: English adopted the French adjective, respelled it with ous, and extended it to people who refuse to explain themselves.
items.cn: 英语借入这个法语形容词，改写成带 ous 的形式，并把词义扩展到「不肯解释自己的人」。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the noun, the adverb and other words on the same Greek stem; the near-meaning group collects adjectives for what cannot be explained.
note.cn: 形近组收同出希腊词根的名词、副词及其他同族词；近义组收表示「无法解释」的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for something unexplained or kept secret.
entries.definitionCN: 表示无法解释或被人保密之事的名称。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in a way that cannot be explained.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，意为「神秘地、莫名其妙地」。

entries.definition: The quality of being strange and unexplained.
entries.definitionCN: 神秘、难以解释的性质。

entries.definition: To puzzle someone completely, from the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 使人完全困惑，同出这一词干。

entries.definition: A person who seeks direct union with the divine.
entries.definitionCN: 追求与神直接合一的人；神秘的。

entries.definition: Unusual and hard to account for, but without the hint of hidden meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 不寻常、难以说明，但没有「背后另有隐情」的暗示。

entries.definition: Hard to understand because the pieces do not fit.
entries.definitionCN: 因线索拼不起来而令人费解。

entries.definition: Deliberately or naturally hard to read, like a riddle.
entries.definitionCN: 像谜语一样难以看透，可指有意为之。

entries.definition: Simply not yet accounted for, without any aura.
entries.definitionCN: 只是尚未得到解释，不带神秘气氛。

normalIntro.en: The word is the adjective of a Greek noun for closed rites, and its relatives still circle around secrets.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是希腊语中表示秘仪的名词的形容词形式，它的同族词至今仍围绕「秘密」打转。

normal.en: Greek myein meant to close the eyes or lips, so mysterious begins with the image of a mouth kept shut.
normal.cn: 希腊语 myein 意为闭上眼或闭上嘴，所以 mysterious 的起点是一张闭紧的嘴。

normal.en: Mystery is the noun and mysterious the adjective; adding ous turns a secret into a quality.
normal.cn: mystery 是名词，mysterious 是形容词；加上 ous，就把一个秘密变成了一种性质。

normal.en: The ending is said quickly as -əs, which is why the last syllable almost disappears in speech.
normal.cn: 词尾读得很轻，接近 -əs，所以最后一个音节在口语里几乎听不见。

normal.en: Mystify is the verb of the same family: to make someone feel they are facing a closed door.
normal.cn: mystify 是同一族的动词：让人觉得自己面对的是一扇关着的门。

normal.en: Mysterious circumstances and a mysterious smile both keep the facts just out of reach.
normal.cn: mysterious circumstances 与 a mysterious smile 都让事实停在伸手够不到的地方。

abstract.en: A door left ajar is more disturbing than a door locked tight, because the gap promises something behind it.
abstract.cn: 虚掩的门比紧锁的门更让人不安，因为那道缝许诺了门后有东西。

abstract.en: Every closed rite and every unopened letter teaches the same lesson about hidden knowledge.
abstract.cn: 每一场闭门仪式、每一封未拆的信，都在讲同一件关于隐秘知识的事。

abstract.en: A word that began with shut lips ends by describing the face of someone who will not answer.
abstract.cn: 一个从「闭紧嘴唇」开始的词，最后用来形容一张不肯回答的脸。

examples.en: A mysterious figure was seen near the gate last night.
examples.cn: 昨夜有人在门附近看见一个神秘的身影。

examples.en: The case remains mysterious after thirty years.
examples.cn: 三十年后这桩案子依然扑朔迷离。

examples.en: He gave a mysterious smile and changed the subject.
examples.cn: 他神秘地笑了笑，换了话题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「密斯特瑞斯」——把秘密密起来，脸上就带出神秘；mysterious 就是神秘的。

root: 希腊语 myein（闭口、闭眼）构成 mysterion（秘仪），经拉丁语 mysterium 与法语 mysterieux 进入英语；一般认为词根与「闭合」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what is shut away from view; the senses spread from unexplained events to sacred hidden power and to people who hide their own reasons.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被关在视线之外」；义项从无法解释的事件，扩展到隐秘的神圣力量，再转到有意藏起自己理由的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door opened only a crack, with a light inside that cannot be made out.
core.cn: 核心意象：只开一道缝的门，里面有看不清的光。

branches.en: a lamp left burning in an empty house
branches.cn: 空屋里一直亮着的灯

branches.en: a footprint that stops halfway across a room
branches.cn: 走到房间中间就断掉的脚印

branches.en: a rite held behind a curtain
branches.cn: 帘子后面举行的仪式

branches.en: milk souring overnight in a valley
branches.cn: 山谷里一夜变坏的牛奶

branches.en: an answer that slides away from the question
branches.cn: 绕开问题的回答

intro.en: The word is built from a Greek verb of closing, its noun of secret rites, a Latin borrowing, and an English adjective ending.
intro.cn: 这个词由希腊语表「闭合」的动词、其表示秘仪的名词、拉丁语的借形，以及一个英语形容词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin took the Greek noun as mysterium and formed mysticus from the same root, and both stand behind the English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把希腊语名词借作 mysterium，又用同一词根造出 mysticus，两者都支撑着英语这一族词。

items.meaning: to close the eyes or lips
full of, having the nature of
hard to explain, full of hidden meaning

definition_zh: 车辆；交通工具；（思想、信息的）传播媒介、手段；载体
definition_en: a machine with wheels or an engine used for transport, or a means of expressing something
core_image: 一辆车停在站台边，门一开，车上的人和想法一起下车
scene: 早高峰的马路上一排车缓缓挪动，尾灯连成一条红线。 No vehicle is allowed on this narrow path.
sceneCN: 这里 vehicle 是「车辆」（第 1 个义项：有轮或有发动机的运输工具）；句意为这条窄路上不允许车辆通行。站台边停着的那辆车，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：车辆、交通工具；传播媒介、手段；载体

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「车辆的、车辆使用的」
名词短语，义为「车辆交通」

senses.title: A machine for transport
senses.titleCN: 车辆：能载人载货的机器
senses.definition: a machine with wheels or an engine used to carry people or goods
senses.definitionCN: 有轮或发动机、用来载人或载货的机器
senses.example: No vehicle is allowed on this narrow path.
senses.exampleCN: 这条窄路上不允许车辆通行。
senses.why: Latin vehiculum named a plain means of carrying, and the road sense grew from it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vehiculum 原指一种朴素的「搬运手段」，道路上的含义由此长出来。

senses.title: A means of expression
senses.titleCN: 表达手段：让思想能走动的载体
senses.definition: a way or medium through which ideas or feelings are expressed
senses.definitionCN: 使思想或感情得以表达的方式或媒介
senses.example: The novel served as a vehicle for her views on education.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说成了她表达教育观点的载体。
senses.why: What carries goods also carries ideas; the word moves from wheels to words.
senses.whyCN: 能载货的东西也能载思想；这个词从车轮走到了文字。

senses.title: A medium of transmission
senses.titleCN: 传播媒介：把信息或物质送到别处
senses.definition: a substance or channel that carries something to another place
senses.definitionCN: 把某物带到别处的物质或渠道
senses.example: Water is a common vehicle for disease in crowded cities.
senses.exampleCN: 在拥挤的城市里，水常是疾病的传播媒介。
senses.why: The word is neutral about what is carried: people, ideas or germs.
senses.whyCN: 这个词对载着什么保持中立：可以是人、思想或病菌。

senses.title: A medium in art and science
senses.titleCN: 溶剂、调色媒介：科学艺术里承载别物的东西
senses.definition: a liquid in which a substance is carried, as in paint or medicine
senses.definitionCN: 承载其他物质的液体，如颜料或药物里的媒介
senses.example: The pigments are held in an oil vehicle before the paint dries.
senses.exampleCN: 颜料在干之前由油性媒介承载。
senses.why: In a workshop the word returns to its plainest sense: something liquid does the carrying.
senses.whyCN: 在作坊里，这个词回到最朴素的意思：由一种液体来承担搬运。

intro.en: Vehicle comes from Latin vehiculum, a means of carrying, built from the verb vehere, to carry.
intro.cn: vehicle 来自拉丁语 vehiculum「搬运手段」，出自动词 vehere「运载」。

items.en: The verb vehere meant to carry or convey, said of riders, ships and carts.
items.cn: 动词 vehere 意为运载，用于骑手、船只和车。

items.en: Its noun vehiculum named any means of transport, not only a machine.
items.cn: 其名词 vehiculum 指任何运输手段，不只是机器。

items.en: French kept véhicule for carts and carriages, and English borrowed that sense.
items.cn: 法语保留 véhicule 指车马，英语借入的就是这一含义。

items.en: With the motor car the street sense tightened into vehicles on wheels.
items.cn: 随着汽车出现，日常含义收窄为带轮子的车辆。

items.en: At the same time the older sense of a carrier widened again into ideas and media.
items.cn: 与此同时，「承载物」的旧义又扩展开来，用于思想与媒介。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the veh- carrying stem; the near-meaning group holds transport words and carriers.
note.cn: 形近组沿表示「运载」的 veh- 词干；近义组收交通与承载相关的词。

entries.definition: Of or for vehicles; the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「车辆的」，是本词的形容词形式。

entries.definition: A blood vessel; sounds close but shares no root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「血管」，音近但不同根。

entries.definition: To carry something across; formed with con-.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「运送、传达」，同一拉丁词根加 con-。

entries.definition: A journey by sea; from the same carrying verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「航行」，出自同一个运载动词。

entries.definition: A passenger road vehicle, the everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小汽车」，最日常的说法。

entries.definition: The whole system of moving people and goods.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「运输」，指整套运送系统。

entries.definition: A channel for ideas or messages, the abstract sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「媒介」，即抽象的含义。

entries.definition: One that carries, used of people, bags or germs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「携带者」，用于人、袋子或病菌。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the carrying root and the double life of the word as transport and as medium.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「运载」词根，以及这个词作为交通工具与媒介的双重身份。

normal.en: Vehicle comes from a Latin verb meaning to carry.
normal.cn: vehicle 出自一个意为「运载」的拉丁动词。

normal.en: Motor vehicle is the formal term in law and insurance.
normal.cn: motor vehicle 是法律与保险里的正式说法。

normal.en: A vehicle for change is a means, not a machine.
normal.cn: a vehicle for change 指手段，不是机器。

normal.en: Convey and voyage share the same root as vehicle.
normal.cn: convey 与 voyage 和 vehicle 同根。

normal.en: The plural is vehicles, with the k sound kept before the s.
normal.cn: 复数是 vehicles，k 音在 s 前仍然保留。

abstract.en: Everything in the word is about being carried: a body, an idea, a germ, a colour.
abstract.cn: 这个词说的全是「被载着」：身体、想法、病菌、颜色。

abstract.en: A vehicle changes the reach of what it carries; the idea is the same size, the audience is not.
abstract.cn: 交通工具改变的是所载之物的抵达范围；想法没变大，听众变大了。

abstract.en: The oldest sense was any means; modern life narrowed it to wheels and then quietly reopened it.
abstract.cn: 最古老的含义是任何手段；现代生活把它收窄到车轮，又悄悄打开。

examples.en: All vehicles must stop at the red light.
examples.cn: 所有车辆必须在红灯前停下。

examples.en: The film became a vehicle for young actors.
examples.cn: 这部电影成了年轻演员展示自己的载体。

examples.en: Mosquitoes are a vehicle for several diseases.
examples.cn: 蚊子是几种疾病的传播媒介。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「为爱扣」——为爱扣上车门，一路载着走：车辆

root: 源自拉丁语名词 vehiculum「运输手段」（动词 vehere「运载」），经法语 véhicule 进入英语；同族词有 convey、voyage、vehicular。

sensesIntro.en: Vehicle begins as anything that carries, narrows to cars, then widens back to ideas, germs and paint.
sensesIntro.cn: vehicle 起初指一切运载之物，收窄为车辆，又扩回思想、病菌与颜料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cart at the platform, doors open, passengers and their plans getting off together.
core.cn: 核心意象：站台边的一辆车，门一开，乘客和他们的计划一起下来。

branches.en: ROAD LINE: machines with wheels or engines.
branches.cn: 道路线：有轮或发动机的机器。

branches.en: ART LINE: a story that carries a point of view.
branches.cn: 艺术线：承载观点的小说或影片。

branches.en: CHANNEL LINE: water or insects carrying disease.
branches.cn: 渠道线：带病的水或昆虫。

branches.en: PAINT LINE: the liquid that holds pigment.
branches.cn: 颜料线：承载颜料的媒介。

branches.en: CONTRAST: transport is the system, a vehicle is one machine in it.
branches.cn: 对照线：transport 是系统，vehicle 是其中一台机器。

intro.en: Vehicle is a Latin noun; its relatives mostly come from the same carrying verb with other prefixes.
intro.cn: vehicle 是拉丁名词，亲属词多由同一运载动词加不同前缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is vehere, to carry, giving vehiculum and also vector and convehere.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础是 vehere「运载」，派生出 vehiculum，也派生出 vector 与 convehere。

items.example: It is the core of vehicle.
It names the thing that carries.
It is the same journey idea.
items.exampleCN: 它带有同样的旅程观念。

definition_zh: 电影院；电影（总称）；电影业
definition_en: a building where films are shown; films in general; the film industry
core_image: 黑暗的大厅里，一束光投在宽银幕上
scene: 周六下午，我和同学约好去看新上映的动画片。 The new cinema opened near our school.
sceneCN: 这里 cinema 是「电影院」（第 1 个义项：放映电影的地方）；句意是学校附近新开了一家电影院。

derivatives.zh: 由 cinema 加后缀 -ic 构成，义为「电影的；电影般的」
英语固有说法，义为「电影；胶片」，与 cinema 同义场

senses.title: A building where films are shown
senses.definition: a place with a screen and seats for watching films
senses.definitionCN: 设有银幕和座位、供观看电影的场所
senses.example: The cinema near the park shows cartoons on weekends.
senses.exampleCN: 公园附近的电影院周末放动画片。
senses.why: The concrete sense names the venue itself.
senses.whyCN: 具体义项直接命名了这个场所。

senses.title: Films as an art form
senses.definition: movies considered together as an art
senses.definitionCN: 作为艺术门类的电影整体
senses.example: She studies the history of world cinema.
senses.exampleCN: 她研究世界电影史。
senses.why: Many works shown in that hall became a whole art named after it.
senses.whyCN: 在那座厅堂里放映的众多作品汇成一门以它命名的艺术。

senses.title: The film industry
senses.definition: the business of making and showing films
senses.definitionCN: 制作和放映电影这一行业
senses.example: He hopes to work in cinema one day.
senses.exampleCN: 他希望有朝一日进入电影业。
senses.why: The art grows into an industry carrying the same name.
senses.whyCN: 这门艺术长大后成为行业，沿用同一名称。

intro.en: Cinema comes from a Greek word for movement, through French.
intro.cn: cinema 源自希腊语表示「运动」的词，经法语传入。

items.en: Greek kinema meant movement, built on kinein, to move.
items.cn: 希腊语 kinema 义为「运动」，词基 kinein 即「移动」。

items.en: French formed cinematographe, the Lumiere brothers' film projector.
items.cn: 法语造出 cinematographe，即卢米埃尔兄弟的电影放映机。

items.en: English clipped it to cinema at the end of the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪末英语将其简化为 cinema。

items.en: It first named the projector, then the hall, then the art.
items.cn: 它先指放映机，后指放映厅，再指电影艺术。

items.en: British English keeps cinema for the movie theatre today.
items.cn: 如今英式英语用 cinema 指电影院。

note.en: The first group gathers moving-picture words; the second gathers look-alikes.
note.cn: 第一组收电影类词，第二组收形近词。

entries.definition: Related to films.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电影的」，是 cinema 加 -ic。

entries.definition: A device for taking photos or films.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「相机；摄像机」，与 cinema 同源。

entries.definition: A spicy powder for cooking.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「肉桂」，读音与 cinema 相近。

entries.definition: A place for stage plays.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「剧院」，演舞台剧的场所。

entries.definition: A film, American usage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电影」，美式说法。

entries.definition: The surface films are shown on.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「银幕」，影院的核心设备。

normalIntro.en: Remember cinema through its Greek move-root.
normalIntro.cn: 通过希腊语「运动」词根记忆 cinema。

normal.en: kinema means movement; films are moving pictures.
normal.cn: kinema 义为运动，电影就是会动的画面。

normal.en: camera and cinematic share the same root.
normal.cn: camera 和 cinematic 与它同根。

normal.en: British usage says go to the cinema.
normal.cn: 英式说法是 go to the cinema。

normal.en: American English says go to the movies.
normal.cn: 美式英语说 go to the movies。

normal.en: world cinema means films from all countries.
normal.cn: world cinema 指世界各国的电影。

abstract.en: See the beam of light sweeping over dark heads.
abstract.cn: 想象光束在黑暗的头顶上扫过。

abstract.en: Hear the pop of a soda can before the film starts.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见开场前汽水罐的轻响。

abstract.en: Feel the big screen pulling your eyes into the story.
abstract.cn: 感受大银幕把目光拉进故事里。

examples.en: Our class went to the cinema for Children's Day.
examples.cn: 儿童节那天我们全班去看了电影。

examples.en: Tickets for the new cinema are half price on Tuesday.
examples.cn: 那家新影院周二半价。

examples.en: Chinese cinema is famous around the world.
examples.cn: 中国电影享誉世界。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「辛妮玛」——辛妮牵着玛莎进影院，看一部会动的画。

root: 希腊语 kinema（运动，词基 kinein「移动」）→ 法语 cinématographe → 十九世纪末英语 cinema；同根词有 camera（摄影机）、cinematic（电影般的）、kinetic（动的）。

sensesIntro.en: Cinema grows from a hall for moving pictures to the art and industry of film.
sensesIntro.cn: cinema 从放映「活动画面」的厅堂成长为电影艺术与产业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark hall where pictures move
core.cn: 核心意象：画面流动的黑暗大厅

branches.en: The movie theatre
branches.cn: 电影院本身

branches.en: Film as an art
branches.cn: 作为艺术的电影

branches.en: The film business
branches.cn: 电影产业

branches.en: A weekend leisure place
branches.cn: 周末休闲场所

branches.en: The history of film
branches.cn: 电影的历史长河

intro.en: The Greek move-root kine- powers a whole word family.
intro.cn: 希腊语词根 kine-（动）撑起了整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Greek kinein is not Latin, but it feeds many English words.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 kinein 虽非拉丁语，却哺育了许多英语词。

items.example: My camera is in the bag.
Two cinemas stand on this street.

definition_zh: 西方的；西部的；（Western）西方国家的；名词：西部片
definition_en: in or from the west, or belonging to Europe and North America
core_image: 太阳落到地图左半边，那边是西，人和风都从那一侧来
scene: 傍晚太阳压在地平线上，整片天烧成橙色。 They drove west along the coast road until the light failed.
sceneCN: 这里 west 是「西方、西面」（第 1 个义项：太阳落下的方向）；句意为他们沿滨海公路向西开，直到天光消失。

pos.zh: 形容词：西方的、西部的；西方国家（尤指欧美）的
名词：西部影片、西部小说（常大写 Western）

derivatives.zh: 词根本身，义为「西、西方；西部的」
加 -er 构成，义为「西方人；西方居民」
加最高级后缀构成，义为「最西端的」
加 -ward 构成，义为「向西的」

senses.title: In or from the west
senses.titleCN: 西方的：位于或来自西边的
senses.definition: situated in the west, or coming from the west
senses.definitionCN: 位于西侧，或来自西边的
senses.example: The western half of the island is wetter and greener.
senses.exampleCN: 岛上的西半部更潮湿、更青绿。
senses.why: The adjective simply takes the compass word west and adds -ern, as in eastern and southern: it names a position on the compass.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把方位词 west 加上后缀 -ern（如同 eastern、southern），表示罗盘上的位置。

senses.title: Belonging to the West
senses.titleCN: 西方国家的：属于欧美的
senses.definition: belonging to Europe and North America, especially their shared culture and institutions
senses.definitionCN: 属于欧洲与北美，尤指其共同文化与制度
senses.example: She studied western philosophy before turning to Chinese classics.
senses.exampleCN: 她先学西方哲学，后来转向中国典籍。
senses.why: Here the word is capitalised in use and means a civilisation, not a compass point: the West as a cultural region.
senses.whyCN: 这里该词实际常大写，指一种文明而非罗盘方向：作为文化区域的「西方」。

senses.title: Facing west
senses.definition: facing towards the west
senses.definitionCN: 面朝西边
senses.example: The western windows catch the last of the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 朝西的窗户能接住最后的阳光。
senses.why: A building or room is described by the side the compass says it faces; the meaning turns from origin to orientation.
senses.whyCN: 建筑物或房间按罗盘所指的朝向描述；词义从「来源」转为「朝向」。

senses.title: The western film
senses.titleCN: 西部片：以美国西部为背景的影片
senses.definition: as a noun, a film or novel about cowboys and settlers in the American West
senses.definitionCN: 名词用法，指以美国西部牛仔与拓荒者为题材的电影或小说
senses.example: He watched an old western on Sunday afternoons.
senses.exampleCN: 他周日下午看一部老西部片。
senses.why: The adjective, used as a noun, names a genre: the stories set in the American West, and the word for the direction became the word for that world.
senses.whyCN: 形容词用作名词就指一种类型：以美国西部为背景的故事，于是表示方向的词成了那个世界的名字。

senses.title: Western as opposed to eastern practice
senses.titleCN: 西式的：与东方做法相对的
senses.definition: used to mark the European or American form of something, as in western medicine
senses.definitionCN: 用于标示某事物欧美式的形态，如 western medicine（西医）
senses.example: The clinic combines western medicine with herbal treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所把西医与草药治疗结合起来。
senses.why: In compounds the word becomes a label of method: it says which tradition a practice comes from, not where it is done.
senses.whyCN: 在复合词中这个词成了方法的标签：它说明某种做法源自哪种传统，而非在哪里做。

intro.en: Western is an Old English adjective formed on west, the direction of sunset, with the -ern ending seen in eastern and southern.
intro.cn: western 是古英语形容词，由表示日落方向的 west 加后缀 -ern 构成，与 eastern、southern 同类。

items.en: Westerne meant 'western, lying to the west', built on west with the adjective ending -erne.
items.cn: 古英语 westerne 意为「西方的、在西边的」，由 west 加形容词词尾 -erne 构成。

items.en: The base west is a Germanic word for the direction of sunset, so the adjective belongs to the oldest layer of the vocabulary.
items.cn: 本词 west 是日耳曼语中表示日落方向的词，因此该形容词属于最古老的词汇层。

items.en: West itself named the direction of the setting sun, a word shared by the Germanic languages.
items.cn: west 本身指日落的方位，是日耳曼诸语言共有的词。

items.en: The spelling became western, and the word was used for winds, shores and parts of a country.
items.cn: 拼写演变为 western，用于西风、西岸以及一国的西半部。

items.en: From the sixteenth century it also named the lands of Europe and America as a group, and later the cowboy film.
items.cn: 自十六世纪起，它也用来统称欧美诸国，后来又指牛仔电影。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other compass adjectives and the family of west; the near-meaning group gathers words for the West as a region.
note.cn: 形近组收其他方位形容词与 west 一族词；近义组收表示「西方」这一区域的词。

entries.definition: The matching adjective for the east.
entries.definitionCN: 同类形容词，义为「东方的」。

entries.definition: The matching adjective for the north.
entries.definitionCN: 同类形容词，义为「北方的」。

entries.definition: Towards the west; an adverb, not an adjective of place.
entries.definitionCN: 同根副词，义为「向西」。

entries.definition: A person from the West; the derived noun.
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，义为「西方人」。

entries.definition: The direction itself; the noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「西」，是形容词背后的方位词。

entries.definition: A formal word for western, from Latin for the setting sun.
entries.definitionCN: 正式用语，义为「西方的」，源自拉丁语「日落」。

entries.definition: Narrower: of Europe only, without America.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，范围更窄，只指欧洲。

entries.definition: Travelling towards the west, said of traffic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「向西行驶的」，多用于交通。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English root west and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语词根 west，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: West is where the sun sets; western is the side it sets on.
normal.cn: west 是太阳落下的地方；western 就是日落的那一侧。

normal.en: The -ern ending turns a compass point into an adjective, as in eastern and southern.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ern 把方位词变成形容词，如 eastern、southern。

normal.en: Capitalised, the West means Europe and North America as a culture.
normal.cn: 大写时 the West 指作为文化整体的欧美。

normal.en: A western is a film about the American West.
normal.cn: a western 指一部关于美国西部的电影。

normal.en: Western medicine stands opposite Chinese medicine in the phrase.
normal.cn: western medicine 在说法上与中医相对。

abstract.en: Stand facing the sunset: everything on your left hand is west.
abstract.cn: 面朝日落站着：左手边的一切都是西。

abstract.en: The word moves from a direction to a civilisation without changing shape.
abstract.cn: 这个词从一个方向滑向一种文明，形态却不变。

abstract.en: Every map makes its own centre, so western is always western relative to a chosen standpoint.
abstract.cn: 每张地图都有自己的中心，所以 western 总是相对于某个既定位置而言的西方。

examples.en: Western Australia is the largest state in the country.
examples.cn: 西澳大利亚是这个国家最大的州。

examples.en: The museum has a fine collection of western paintings.
examples.cn: 这家博物馆收藏了不少西方绘画佳作。

examples.en: They spent the evening watching an old western.
examples.cn: 他们整个晚上都在看一部老西部片。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪死疼」——往西走的人被风吹得歪得要死要疼：西边的

root: 古英语 west「日落的方向、西」→ westerne「西边的」→ 英语 western；同族词有 west、westerner、westernmost、westward。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of western run from a compass position to a civilisation: lying to the west, belonging to the West, facing west, a cowboy film, and a label for method.
sensesIntro.cn: western 的五个义项从方位走到文明：位于西边、属于欧美、朝西、西部片，以及标示方法的西式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the sun going down on the left half of the map.
core.cn: 核心意象：太阳落到地图左半边。

branches.en: THE POSITION: the western half of a place.
branches.cn: 位置线：一个地方的西半部。

branches.en: THE CIVILISATION: Europe and America as the West.
branches.cn: 文明线：作为「西方」的欧美。

branches.en: THE ORIENTATION: western windows take the last sun.
branches.cn: 朝向线：朝西的窗户接住最后的阳光。

branches.en: THE GENRE: a western is a film of the American West.
branches.cn: 类型线：a western 是美国西部的影片。

branches.en: THE METHOD: western medicine names a tradition.
branches.cn: 方法线：western medicine 指一种传统。

intro.en: Western is a native English adjective; the -ern ending and the -er of westerner do the work.
intro.cn: western 是英语本族形容词；起作用的是后缀 -ern 与 westerner 中的 -er。

latinIntro.en: West is Germanic, not Latin; only the scholarly doublet occidental comes through Latin occidens, the setting sun.
latinIntro.cn: west 属日耳曼语而非拉丁语；只有学究气的同义词 occidental 来自拉丁语 occidens「日落」。

items.example: It is the base noun of the family.
It forms western, as in eastern.
It gives occidental, the Latin-side word for western.
items.exampleCN: 它生出 occidental，即拉丁系的「西方」。

definition_zh: 敲；敲门；碰撞；撞倒；敲门声
definition_en: to hit a door or surface with the hand or an object, often to be let in, or to strike something and make it fall or move
core_image: 指节落在木门上，发出短促的三下响声
scene: 旅馆的木门半旧，走廊里亮着一盏昏黄的灯。 He knocked three times, then waited until a tired voice told him to come in.
sceneCN: 这里 knock 是「敲、敲门」（第 1 个义项：用手或物件敲打门面以示意），句意是他敲了三下，等人用疲倦的声音叫他进去。画面里有旅馆走廊、木门与昏黄的灯。

derivatives.zh: 加 -er 构成，义为「门环、叩门者」
knock 与 out 合成，义为「击倒获胜；出众的人或物」
合成词，义为「可拆装的；压倒性的」
合成词，义为「闹剧式的、粗笨却结实的」

senses.title: To hit a door to be admitted
senses.definition: to strike a door with the hand so that people inside will open it
senses.definitionCN: 用手击门以让里面的人开门
senses.example: Someone knocked at the door just after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 午夜刚过就有人敲门。
senses.why: The core act is a short strike on a hard surface, loud enough to be heard inside.
senses.whyCN: 核心动作是在硬面上短促一击，声音刚好让屋内的人听见。

senses.title: To strike something and hit it
senses.definition: to strike a thing or a person, often by accident or with some force
senses.definitionCN: 撞上某物或某人，常属意外或带有力量
senses.example: The branch knocked against the window all night.
senses.exampleCN: 树枝整夜撞着窗户。
senses.why: From hitting on purpose the word widens to any collision, whether intended or not.
senses.whyCN: 从有意击打扩大为任何碰撞，不论是否有意。

senses.title: To make something fall
senses.definition: to cause something to fall or move by striking it
senses.definitionCN: 击打使某物倒下或移开
senses.example: He knocked the cup off the table.
senses.exampleCN: 他把杯子从桌上撞掉了。
senses.why: A blow that pushes an object off its place is the same action aimed at the thing rather than the door.
senses.whyCN: 把东西打离原位的这一击，用的是同一动作，只是目标换成了物件而非门。

senses.title: A blow or a setback
senses.definition: an act of striking, or a difficulty that sets a person back
senses.definitionCN: 击打的动作，或使人受挫的困难
senses.example: The team took a heavy knock when its captain left.
senses.exampleCN: 队长离开后球队受到沉重打击。
senses.why: The noun keeps the physical blow and turns it into an image of bad luck.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了实实在在的一击，又把它转成厄运的比喻。

senses.title: The sound of knocking
senses.definition: the short sharp sound made by striking a door or a hard surface
senses.definitionCN: 敲击门或硬面所发出的短促响声
senses.example: A sharp knock came from the engine.
senses.exampleCN: 发动机里传来一声尖锐的敲击声。
senses.why: The sound is the most detachable part of the blow, so the word names it on its own.
senses.whyCN: 声音是击打中最能单独剥离的部分，于是这个词也单独指这种声音。

intro.en: Knock first appears in English in the Middle Ages, probably from a Germanic root for striking, and its k has been silent for centuries.
intro.cn: knock 在中世纪才出现于英语，可能源自表示「击打」的日耳曼语词根，词首的 k 已静音数百年。

items.en: The verb is not recorded in Old English, though the related noun cnocc named a lump or knock.
items.cn: 古英语中未记录这个动词，但相关名词 cnocc 指肿块或一击。

items.en: Knock appears in the fourteenth century with the sense of striking hard.
items.cn: knock 于十四世纪出现，义为「重击」。

items.en: A relation with German knacken and Dutch knakken, both meaning to crack, is generally accepted.
items.cn: 普遍认为它与德语 knacken、荷兰语 knakken（意为「裂响」）有关。

items.en: The phrase knock at the door fixes the everyday sense of asking for admittance.
items.cn: knock at the door 这一说法固定了「示意求入」的日常义。

items.en: Particles multiply the senses: knock out, knock down, knock over, and knock off.
items.cn: 小品词使义项增多：knock out、knock down、knock over、knock off。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers silent-k words and relatives; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs of hitting.
note.cn: 形近组收 k 不发音的近形词与同族词；近义组收其他表示「击打」的动词。

entries.definition: Starts with the same silent k and names a tied loop of rope.
entries.definitionCN: 同样以不发音的 k 开头，指绳结。

entries.definition: One letter away, meaning a special skill.
entries.definitionCN: 只差一个字母，意为「窍门、技能」。

entries.definition: The word plus -er, naming a door ring or a person who knocks.
entries.definitionCN: 本词加 -er，指门环或叩门者。

entries.definition: To touch lightly and quickly, much softer than a knock.
entries.definitionCN: 轻而快地触及，比 knock 轻得多。

entries.definition: To hit noisily and heavily, with a louder result.
entries.definitionCN: 重而响地撞击，声音更大。

entries.definition: To hit something with a dull, accidental thud.
entries.definitionCN: 偶然撞上，声音沉闷。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real phrase family, the particle combinations, and the silent k that runs through the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用真实的搭配家族、小品词组合，以及贯穿全词的不发音 k。

normal.en: The k stays silent, as in knee, knife and knot.
normal.cn: k 不发音，和 knee、knife、knot 一样。

normal.en: Knock at the door is the phrase for asking to come in.
normal.cn: knock at the door 是请求进屋的说法。

normal.en: Particles change the result: out is a fight, down is a fall, over is a spill.
normal.cn: 小品词改变结果：out 是打斗，down 是倒下，over 是打翻。

normal.en: Two negatives make a compliment: she is a knock-out.
normal.cn: 两重否定反成赞语：她是惊艳众人的人。

normal.en: A knock on the engine is a warning sound, not a touch.
normal.cn: 发动机里的 knock 是警告声，不是触碰。

abstract.en: A knock is a question asked in sound, and the silence after it is the answer.
abstract.cn: 敲门是用声音提出的问题，之后的那片安静就是回答。

abstract.en: Any collision is a knock, because the same short shock passes through two objects.
abstract.cn: 任何碰撞都是一次 knock，因为同一股短促的冲击从两个物体之间传过。

abstract.en: From a fist on wood to a setback in life, the word keeps the image of something arriving suddenly.
abstract.cn: 从拳头落上木板到人生受挫，这个词始终保留着「突然到来」的意象。

examples.en: Please knock before you enter the office.
examples.cn: 进办公室之前请先敲门。

examples.en: The wind knocked the flowerpot off the sill.
examples.cn: 风把花盆从窗台上撞了下来。

examples.en: There was a loud knock at the back door.
examples.cn: 后门上响起一声很响的敲击。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「闹克」——指节一闹，门就咚咚克响

root: 中古英语 knocken（始见于十四世纪，义为「重击」），可能源自日耳曼语中表示裂响的词根，与德语 knacken、荷兰语 knakken 相关；词首 k 不发音，后靠小品词扩展出 knock out、knock down 等义。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: knocking on a door, any striking collision, causing something to fall, a hit as a setback, and the sound itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：敲门，任何撞击，把东西撞倒，作为挫折的一击，以及那种敲击声。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: knuckles striking a wooden door, three short sounds in the quiet.
core.cn: 核心意象：指节落在木门上，安静里响起三下短声。

branches.en: THE DOOR LINE: a knock is a request to be let in.
branches.cn: 门线：敲门是请求被放进来。

branches.en: THE IMPACT LINE: anything struck may move, fall or break.
branches.cn: 冲击线：被击中的东西会移动、倒下或破碎。

branches.en: THE FORTUNE LINE: a blow becomes a setback in life.
branches.cn: 命运线：一击变成人生里的挫折。

branches.en: THE SOUND LINE: the noise of the blow can stand alone.
branches.cn: 声音线：击打的声音可以单独成义。

branches.en: THE FORM LINE: the silent k ties it to knee and knot.
branches.cn: 形式线：不发音的 k 把它与 knee、knot 连在一起。

intro.en: Knock is a Germanic verb that English expands mainly through particles and compounds, not affixes.
intro.cn: knock 是日耳曼动词，英语主要通过小品词与合成来扩展它，而非词缀。

latinIntro.en: Knock has no Latin source; the Latin striking words below are contrasts.
latinIntro.cn: knock 没有拉丁语来源，下面这些拉丁语击打词只是对照。

items.example: He was knocked out in round two.
They knocked down the old wall.
The cat knocked over the vase.

items.meaning: one who or a thing that

definition_zh: 改变；更换；交换；零钱；找零；变化
definition_en: to make or become different; to replace one thing with another; money in small coins; the money returned after paying
core_image: 把旧硬币换成新纸币，或换下旧校服换上新装
scene: 换季了，周末妈妈帮我把秋装收进柜子，换上冬装。 Mom helped me change my clothes for the colder weather.
sceneCN: 这里 change 是「更换」（第 2 个义项：以新换旧）；句意为妈妈帮我换上了保暖的冬装。

derivatives.zh: 由 change 加 -able 构成，义为「易变的；可变的」
由 ex- 加 change 构成，义为「交换；交易」
由 change 加 over 构成，义为「转换；变更」

senses.title: To make or become different
senses.definition: to make someone or something different, or to become different
senses.definitionCN: 使不同，或自身变得不同
senses.example: Autumn changes the colour of the leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 秋天改变了树叶的颜色。
senses.why: The old sense of trading places, time after time, grows into the general idea of becoming other.
senses.whyCN: 古义指轮换换班，一次次交替便生长为「变为他物」的普遍概念。

senses.title: To replace one thing with another
senses.definition: to take off one thing and put on or use another
senses.definitionCN: 取下一物，换上或改用另一物
senses.example: Mom helped me change my clothes for the colder weather.
senses.exampleCN: 天气转冷，妈妈帮我换上了冬装。
senses.why: Exchanging one for another is the most concrete form of making different.
senses.whyCN: 以一换一正是「使之不同」最具体的形式。

senses.title: To give and receive one thing for another
senses.definition: to give one thing and receive another in return
senses.definitionCN: 交出某物并换取另一物
senses.example: We changed seats so everyone could see.
senses.exampleCN: 我们交换了座位，让每个人都能看见。
senses.why: The oldest sense was barter: two parties each hand over what they hold.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义是物物交换：双方各自交出手中之物。

senses.title: Money in small coins
senses.definition: coins of low value, or money in small units
senses.definitionCN: 低面额硬币或小额货币
senses.example: I keep some small change for the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 我留着些零钱坐公交。
senses.why: Money broken into smaller pieces is 'changed' money, carrying the exchange sense into coins.
senses.whyCN: 被化整为零的钱是「换过」的钱，交换之义便落在了硬币上。

senses.title: The money returned after paying
senses.definition: the money given back when you pay more than the price
senses.definitionCN: 付款超过价格时被退回的钱
senses.example: Here is your change, sir.
senses.exampleCN: 先生，这是找您的零钱。
senses.why: The seller exchanges what you gave for what is owed back, the last echo of barter.
senses.whyCN: 卖家把你多付的换回应退的款项，是物物交换的最后回声。

intro.en: Change comes from a Late Latin word for exchanging, arriving through Old French.
intro.cn: change 源自晚期拉丁语中指交换的词，经古法语传入英语。

items.en: Late Latin cambiare meant to exchange, to barter one thing for another.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 cambiare 指交换、以物易物。

items.en: Old French changier meant to exchange, replace or alter.
items.cn: 古法语 changier 指交换、替换或更改。

items.en: Middle English chaungen covered altering things and switching roles.
items.cn: 中古英语 chaungen 涵盖改变事物与轮换职位。

items.en: The money senses grew as trade and small coins spread.
items.cn: 随着贸易与硬币普及，钱币诸义生长起来。

items.en: Modern English keeps changing things, coins, and money returned.
items.cn: 现代英语保留改变、硬币与找零诸义。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects altering and money words.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收改变与钱币类词。

entries.definition: An opportunity or possibility.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「机会」，拼写与 change 仅差一字母。

entries.definition: To ask money for something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「收费」，拼写与 change 相近。

entries.definition: To give and receive in return.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「交换」，由 change 加 ex- 构成。

entries.definition: To make something slightly different.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「改动」，与 change 相近但幅度较小。

entries.definition: To put a new thing in place of an old one.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「替换」，与 change 的更换义相近。

entries.definition: Small pieces of metal money.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「硬币」，与 change 的零钱义相近。

normalIntro.cn: 借助词根与词族记忆 change。

abstract.en: Feel the old uniform giving way to the new one.
abstract.cn: 感受旧校服脱下、新校服上身。
